items.title: In New Mexico, a river runs through ‘the middle of a hellscape’
items.summary_raw: It’s an early May afternoon, and Charlie Barrett has parked his pickup in a pullout along a county road a few hundred feet from the Black River in southern New Mexico, just a mile from where it empties into the Pecos River. He has stopped to set up a video camera that detects heat and gasses invisible to the eye to check for emissions at a nearby oil and gas operation. Stepping out of the truck, Barrett finds the pullout muddy and dotted with puddles — an anomaly during an ongoing drought. A gray chunk of salt the size of a medicine ball sits near a mud puddle flecked with shimmering, white crystals. “Unfortunately this is pretty common,” he said. “It’s also quite dangerous.” It appeared that someone had dumped oilfield wastewater — also known as produced water — at the pullout. The extremely saline and toxic byproduct of oil and gas production carries a mix of petroleum compounds and oilfield chemicals. Produced water can be radioactive, too. Barrett said he worries that people would unwittingly drive through the muck or pull off the road and walk through it. All day, every day, hundreds of semi trucks haul the toxic produced water from well sites to disposal stations along the highways and backroads of this far corner of New Mexico. That water is an unwanted byproduct of oil and gas development. More than three barrels of wastewater come out of the ground for every barrel of extracted oil, on average in New Mexico. items.summary_raw: Analytický ústav STEM připravil model pro hypotetické volby do Poslanecké sněmovny, pokud by se konaly na začátku října. Hlavními pohyby od voleb je jednak oslabení podpory hnutí ANO, dále růst hnutí STAN související s poklesem třetí ODS, stagnace hnutí Motoristů sobě kolem pětiprocentní hranice a nástup hnutí Naše Česko, které však nyní zaostává za možným ziskem ze začátku roku. Kdyby se nyní konaly volby do Poslanecké sněmovny, vyhrálo by s velkým náskokem 31,3 % hnutí ANO, které od voleb ale část podpory ztratilo. S odstupem druhé by bylo se 16,6 % hnutí STAN, které pokračuje v růstu a vzdaluje se od třetí ODS s 11,3 %. Na čtvrtém místě by se se 7,5 % umístila samostatná SPD a na pátém Piráti se 7,2 %. Motoristé sobě by získali 4,6 %, a zůstávají tak na hraně vstupu do Sněmovny. Ostatní strany a hnutí už by se do hypotetické nově volené Sněmovny samostatně jednoznačně nedostaly. TOP 09 by si připsala 3,7 %, KDU-ČSL 2,5 %, Zelení 2,1 % a hnutí Naše Česko pak 1,9 %. Samostatné PRO i KSČM by získaly shodně 1,8 %. STAČILO!, Svobodní i SOCDEM by se pak dostaly lehce nad 1 %. Ze stran, které nedosahují ani 1 %, pak zmiňme vládní Trikoloru a dále Přísahu či hnutí Generace.

items.title: Fifty billion seedlings: Can Ethiopia replant its ravaged forests?
items.summary_raw: Niku Argane’s farm sits on a steep hillside in central Ethiopia’s semi-mountainous Gurage Zone, where years of flooding have carved deep gullies through the land. Soil that once produced enough barley and potatoes to feed his wife and four children — and left a surplus to sell in the market — has eroded, while drought has made what land remains harder to cultivate. “We have never stopped farming, but our production declined because of land degradation,” the 32-year-old said from his farm in Ambele Kebele. Over the last century, Ethiopia nearly eradicated its forests as trees were cleared for farming, grazing, and fuel. The loss of tree cover and tree roots allowed wind and rain to wash away fertile topsoil and contributed to declining crop yields. That vulnerability is now being compounded by climate change. Ethiopia is among the countries most vulnerable to its effects: Heavier downpours are sluicing away depleted soils and triggering landslides, while more intense droughts, combined with the loss of shade that trees once provided, rapidly dry out the land. Land degradation costs the country an estimated $4.3 billion a year through smaller harvests and lost income to farmers, which also means there is less food to eat. With more than 100 million Ethiopians dependent on agriculture for their livelihoods, the consequences reach far beyond the environment. items.title: Platforma proti hlubinnému úložišti: SÚRAO opět zrušilo výběrové řízení na geologické vrty
items.summary_raw: Správa úložišť radioaktivních odpadů (SÚRAO) jen několik hodin před termínem pro podání nabídek zrušila další výběrové řízení na realizaci hlubokých geologických vrtů na lokalitách, které vytipovala jako potenciálně vhodné pro hlubinné úložiště vysoce radioaktivních odpadů. Předchozí, takřka rok trvající výběrové řízení na dodavatele prací musela zrušit v prosinci 2025. Nezdá se reálné, že lze ještě stihnout stanovený termín roku 2030 pro výběr finální a záložní lokality hlubinného úložiště, tím méně pak ambiciózní rok 2028, o který usilovala Správa. Klíčovou součástí geologických prací, bez nichž nelze získat potřebná data pro výběr, jsou totiž právě tyto vrty. Platforma proti hlubinnému úložišti se ale obává, že bude vzrůstat tlak na dodržení politického termínu bez ohledu na geologická data z hloubky horninového prostředí.

items.title: “Technology and science are, by definition, non-discriminatory”- narratives of the performance of sex and gender dimensions in European climate project proposals
items.summary_raw: Abstract The integration of sex and gender dimensions (SGDs) in European research and innovation (R&I) funding has become a central policy priority, yet its practical implementation in grant proposals remains underexplored. This study investigates how SGDs are framed, negotiated, and operationalised in technology-oriented proposals addressing the climate crisis, submitted to Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe between 2014 and 2022. Using an inductive constructivist grounded theory approach, 87 funded and rejected proposals were analysed to identify patterns in SGDs integration. The findings reveal three main themes: (i) a wide spectrum of integration practices, ranging from comprehensive incorporation to more procedural or symbolic inclusion; (ii) differences in the use of terminology and conceptual clarity; and (iii) a tendency to conflate equal participation with SGDs in R&I, often focusing on women’s representation while overlooking broader structural dimensions. A tension emerges between formal compliance and substantive engagement, shaped by disciplinary norms, institutional expectations, and policy signals. The study provides a foundational understanding of how SGDs are currently addressed in EU grant writing and highlights areas where further support may be beneficial. These include enhanced training, clearer guidance, more transparent evaluation criteria, and greater institutional support. The findings offer useful insights for policymakers, funders, and researchers…

items.title: The boundaries of global concern: How socioeconomic context shapes the link between global consciousness and environmental attitudes
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate change requires unprecedented international cooperation; yet growing protectionist sentiment poses a significant barrier to collective action. Global Consciousness (GC), a psychological orientation characterized by a connection to humanity and the world as a whole, has been theorized as a key driver of benevolent behaviors, including pro‐environmental attitudes. However, empirical evidence linking GC to environmentalism remains largely confined to specific contexts, leaving the generalizability of this relationship across diverse societies unclear. Leveraging data from the European Values Survey (EVS) and the World Values Survey (WVS), this study examines the link between GC and indicators of environmentalism: confidence, active membership in environmental organizations, and prioritizing environmental protection over economic growth. We further examine whether socioeconomic context moderates this relationship, hypothesizing that the effect of GC on environmental attitudes will be stronger in wealthier nations, as measured by the Human Development Index (HDI). Multilevel models revealed that, across 35 countries in Study 1 ( N = 40,259) and 86 countries in Study 2 ( N = 123,280), GC is consistently and positively associated with environmentalism. Crucially, this relationship is significantly moderated by HDI. These results indicate that the positive effect of GC on environmentalism is stronger in countries with higher socioeconomic progress, suggesting that…

items.summary_raw: Artificial intelligence requires systematic reflection on the relationship between technological progress, collective responsibility and the dignity of the person, making a new social pact necessary. The article links dependence on fossil fuels to geopolitical imbalances, inflationary pressures and the ability of authoritarian regimes to support power policies, proposing international coordination, including at the UN, that reconciles energy security, climate protection and the transition to renewable sources and, in perspective, nuclear fusion. This analysis is accompanied by the criticism of an economy based exclusively on solvency, which excludes needs without adequate purchasing power from the production and distribution of essential goods. To combat poverty, inequality and vulnerability to war, an international agency capable of promoting socially useful work and coordinating the production and distribution of fundamental resources is envisaged. In this framework, artificial intelligence and robotics could contribute to the analysis of needs, the organization of work, agriculture, assistance and scientific research, as long as they remain subordinate to democratic decision-making and criteria of transparency, human control and non-discrimination. Finally, the technological comparison between the United States, China and Europe shows the need, especially for Europe, to strengthen investment, research and regulatory capacity. items.title: A socio-technical analysis of the natural hydrogen hype: Network dynamics and institutional expectation governance
items.summary_raw: Promotional language in scientific and institutional documents is usually dismissed as individual failing or passing fashion. Using Bourdieu's field theory, the Sociology of Expectations and Bacchi's problem representation, we argue instead that it reflects scientific documents' structural position and institutional documents' functional mandate in governance. First, an expert-calibrated Large Language Model scores eight promotional dimensions across 268 natural hydrogen documents (1987-mid-2025). Hype, defined as evidential disproportion rather than forward-looking language, occupies the top two of five levels, whereas the models cover the full scale. Two metrics computed on each document's references translate Bourdieu's field theory into network terms, and both behave as it expects. Low out-closeness centrality, the strongest correlate, places those references at the margins of the field. A high hub score shows reliance on canonical authorities, whose symbolic capital the document borrows. Others are high novelty, absent direct measurements, hydrocarbon-system analogies, lower-prestige journals and a techno-economic or environmental focus, together explaining a third of the variance. The register rises as newcomers enter peripheral positions. Second, discourse analysis of 22 institutional documents (2021–2026) shows that register follows mandate. Enactors amplify expectations and Selectors temper them, as in the Sociology of Expectations. Hybrids, the role added here…

items.title: Cross border consequences of responses to climate change: Risks and opportunities
items.summary_raw: Losses and damages from the impacts of climate change are already reshaping economic development pathways. However, so too are mitigation and adaptation actions taken in response to climate change. As countries implement climate policies with increasing ambition and scale, cross-border effects arise for other countries. Building on evolving conceptualisations of transboundary climate risk we set out a framework to map policy measures, transboundary flow alterations and transmission mechanisms that give rise to international risks and opportunities. Drawing empirically from observable effects across five Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), we identify that climate-related responses in other countries across domains such as energy, industrial, migration and defence policy, can transmit effects through a range of flows (trade, finance, people, biophysical, technology) and mechanisms (prices, production factors, norms, security). Failure to adequately conceptualise how climate responses in one country will affect others, the transmission pathways and channels to respond, has major implications for the current fragile consensus on addressing the climate emergency. New conceptual frameworks to enhance understanding of the channels of impact will better equip policymakers and researchers to anticipate the full spectrum of cross-border spillovers, manage risks governance, and identify opportunities.

items.title: Why the Wilderness Society Backs a Data Center Moratorium
items.summary_raw: This week’s Q&A is with Dan Hartinger, senior policy director for The Wilderness Society, a prominent land conservation organization in D.C. that this week called for a moratorium on data center development on public land. The public statement was relatively scant on details about the group’s stance, and a decade of reporting on policy in Washington has taught me that its positions are quite influential, especially in more traditional outdoor recreation and conservationist circles that are also often bipartisan. So I reached out and asked if someone could further explain the society’s position, and Dan obliged. The following chat was lightly edited for clarity. Let’s start at the beginning. What brought The Wilderness Society to make a call for a moratorium against data centers on public lands? Like many others, we were concerned about news reporting on industrial-scale data centers being proposed on public lands. When we saw the scale of what was proposed – covering tens of thousands of acres of public lands, being pushed through without public input about whether this was an acceptable use of this land – it became clear we needed to hit the brakes and give the public a chance to evaluate this. Our mission and vision for The Wilderness Society is not on the broader debate about AI data centers. It’s on public lands. Those are a shared resource we need to manage for the benefit of all Americans. We need to be careful not to sacrifice those for poorly understood impacts from…

items.title: Dynamic Electricity Pricing Cuts Both Ways for EVs
items.summary_raw: There’s no escape when gas prices spike. You might know a station across town that’s always a dime cheaper per gallon than everybody else, but that’s about the best a driver can hope for. There’s no service station down the street that sells half-price gas after midnight. No Chevron is changing its gas price moment by moment, its big neon sign flashing like a stock ticker. That’s exactly what’s possible as the world moves to electric cars, though. Electricity markets are complex and volatile, responding moment by moment to movements in energy supply and demand, weather, and other factors. Cars, when they’re left plugged in all day or overnight, can take advantage, charging whenever electricity gets cheap. This dynamic environment, offering flexibility in price and in time, opens up money-saving opportunities for EV drivers that were impossible in the one-price-fits-all gasoline days. But it also creates potential drawbacks — at least for those who have fewer choices about when and where they charge. Andrew Peterman, the director of advanced energy solutions at Rivian, touched on this topic last week during the future of mobility session at Heatmap’s New York Climate Week event. Peterman says Rivian owners do 80% to 90% of their charging at home on level 2 plugs, where the vehicle might remain parked for 14 to 16 hours. Suppose you live somewhere like California and you come home from work in the evening. Everyone else is returning home just then, too, turning on their home…

Reaction-based cryo-EM resolves the continuous conformational spectrum of CTP synthase catalysis
items.summary_raw: Capturing enzymes under native turnover conditions remains a grand challenge in structural biology. Here, we develop a reaction-based cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy that directly samples Drosophila melanogaster cytidine triphosphate synthase (CTPS) from actively catalyzing mixtures containing only natural substrates and allosteric effectors. By integrating reaction-based sampling with three-dimensional variability analysis, we resolve a continuous conformational spectrum of CTPS during catalysis. This approach visualizes the chemical progression of 4-phosphoryl-uridine triphosphate (4Pi-UTP) formation and reveals a previously unobserved co-occupancy pattern of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and CTP at the reaction end point. Cross-validation with nonhydrolyzable ATP analogs demonstrates that UTP phosphorylation by ATP, rather than mere ATP binding, shifts the conformational ensemble toward more closed states. Our findings establish reaction-based cryo-EM as a framework for resolving chemically annotated conformational ensembles without predefining a single trapped intermediate.

Understanding consciousness (biological and artificial) as a society of self-schemas
items.summary_raw: This article argues that human cognition is more than the performance of functions such as memory, decision-making, and attention. The brain also builds schematic models of those cognitive functions and uses those models to monitor, predict, and partially control them. When you introspect, your understanding of who you are and what is happening inside of you is derived from those schematic, sometimes inaccurate, but generally useful models, rather than from the actual cognitive functions that are represented by those models. The proposal expands the previously proposed attention schema theory to a more general schema theory, in which the mind as we know it introspectively is a society of interacting self-schemas. The article focuses on five self-schemas including the attention schema (which is proposed to give us our intuitions about a conscious mind that takes possession of items in a vivid manner), a decision schema (which generates simplified, sometimes confabulated accounts of the decision-making process and gives us our intuitive understanding of agency and will), emotion schemas (which create complex interpretations of the physiological state of the body and provide us with our understanding of emotional experience), the body schema (which provides our understanding of who we are as physical beings), and personas (which give us our understanding of our emotional, social, and moral character, and act as a framework to guide our behavior). The article includes a…

items.title: Reply to Roff: Ecological readiness must evolve with AI
GTP orchestrates CTP synthase via an allosteric effector–cycling mechanism
items.summary_raw: Cytidine triphosphate (CTP), a fundamental building block of RNA, plays vital roles in diverse biological processes. CTP synthase (CTPS) is the only known enzyme for de novo synthesis of CTP. Efficient CTPS catalysis requires guanosine triphosphate (GTP) in a dose-dependent, nonconsumptive manner; however, the precise mechanism by which GTP drives CTP formation remains unclear. Here, we integrate a series of cryo-EM structures of Drosophila melanogaster CTPS captured from actively catalyzing samples with biochemical and mutagenesis analyses, yielding 34 distinct CTPS states at resolutions up to 2.0 Å. We find that GTP binds to and dissociates from CTPS once per catalytic cycle, thereby enabling the production of a single CTP molecule. Initial GTP engagement requires formation of 4-phosphoryl-UTP in the AL domain, whereas full stabilization of GTP binding is promoted by occupancy of the GAT active site. Together, these two checkpoints couple GTP recruitment and stabilization to catalytic progress in the two domains, enabling the coordinated synthesis of one CTP molecule per GTP binding–dissociation cycle. Moreover, the GTP-recognition site is highly conserved across the three domains of life. These findings establish a comprehensive mechanistic framework for efficient CTPS catalysis and define “effector-cycling”—in which GTP undergoes obligatory binding and dissociation during each catalytic cycle to regulate an intermediate step in a multistep catalytic process—as a distinct…

items.title: Multiple-oxygen isotope constraints on aerobic respiration and gross primary productivity
items.summary_raw: Primary production on land and in the surface ocean is a critical component of Earth’s carbon and oxygen cycles, controlling the uptake of CO 2 and the release of O 2 to the atmosphere. Quantitative estimates of these O 2 and CO 2 fluxes remain challenging. Of the methods used, the triple-oxygen-isotope analysis of O 2 is considered to provide the most robust in situ estimate of gross productivity. However, this method relies on one key assumption—that the oxygen isotope fractionation of aerobic respiration is constant—and recent experimental studies have shown that it can vary significantly. When applied to the same calculation of gross productivity, the experimentally determined variation in fractionation could produce > 100% error. In this work, the mechanistic origin of the variation in respiratory fractionation is explored using experiments on the model organism Escherichia coli . These experiments suggest that the fractionation is strongly correlated with the cell-specific O 2 consumption rate, weakly correlated with the dissolved-O 2 concentration, and may also depend on the identity of the terminal oxidase enzyme used to reduce O 2 . Modeling suggests that these influences on fractionation are likely to be important in the marine water column, and could produce up to ± 120% error in estimates of gross productivity made using triple-oxygen-isotope analyses. This error may be significantly reduced through concurrent analyses of the “clumped” (multiply substituted)…

items.title: Dystrophic changes of nigrostriatal axons harboring a SYNJ1 Parkinson’s mutation suggest catastrophic failure of endocytic mechanisms
items.summary_raw: Synaptojanin 1 is a brain enriched phosphoinositide phosphatase implicated in endocytosis at the synapse. A mutation (R258Q) that selectively impairs its Sac1 phosphatase domain causes early onset familial Parkinsonism. Neurons of mice with this mutation display synaptic vesicle traffic defects across the brain, but selective dystrophic changes in a subset of dopaminergic axons in the dorsolateral striatum. Using correlative light microscopy-FIB-SEM of mutant mouse striata to visualize in 3D these abnormal structures we show that they represent clusters of focal axonal dilations harboring massive, onion-like DAT enriched plasma membrane infoldings, generally localized next to cell bodies of neighboring cells, often engulfing evaginations of such cells. This dysmorphia was associated with a deficit in dopamine release in the same striatal region. Given the involvement of Synj1 in endocytic mechanisms, these structures may reflect an imbalance between exocytosis and endocytosis. Their occurrence only in a subset of axons suggests a vulnerability threshold of these axons beyond which the expansion of the plasma membrane is not counteracted by compensatory mechanisms.

items.title: How biological synapses self-assemble gradient learning
items.summary_raw: Existing models of learning in the brain explain how given circuits learn, but not how biology could assemble those circuits in the first place. To address this gap, we formulate Self-Assembling Learning—the study of how learning systems can emerge from lower-level interactions—and introduce one example mechanism, the Self-Assembling Motif (SAM). SAM is self-assembling at two scales: The motif emerges from initially random connectivity under heterosynaptic plasticity rules, and networks of SAMs, composed hierarchically, self-organize into dynamics that provably approximate a generalized form of stochastic gradient descent—matching backpropagation-level performance. This suggests that biological learning need not be prescribed but can emerge from local rules—and to a far greater extent than previously thought.

items.title: Interventions to mitigate post-infection morbidity: Management insights from simple models
items.summary_raw: A variety of pathogens that cause acute disease can also affect their host long after recovery. These post-infection effects lead to elevated costs for individuals and societies, which can be mitigated by large-scale interventions. Here, we examine the management of post-infection morbidity with mathematical models. First, we show that long-term usage of nonpharmaceutical interventions can reduce post-acute burden. Second, to investigate how post-infection effects affect optimal vaccination coverage, we generalize and expand on classic epidemiological-economic models. We include post-infection costs, and consider the cost of vaccination as a general increasing function of coverage. If there is some sub-elimination coverage that locally minimizes costs (beyond elimination), we show that the decision of whether to vaccinate or not is independent of the transmission rate (however elimination does depend on this). Echoing existing theoretical results with exponentially increasing costs, we find that if vaccination costs either only accelerate or only decelerate with increased coverage, there is a unique, transmission-independent interior level of vaccination coverage (nonzero and sub-elimination) that locally minimizes or maximizes societal costs, respectively. In all settings, we show that post-infection effects can substantially shift societal incentives toward elimination. Furthermore, when costs of vaccination change concavity, the optimal coverage level is very sensitive to…

items.title: Quantum Fisher information and photon statistics from shift current shot noise
items.summary_raw: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) sets the ultimate precision of optical phase measurements and can reveal multiphoton entanglement. Yet the photon-number fluctuations that encode this sensitivity are difficult to convert into an electrical signal. We theoretically predict that a photodetector utilizing the shot noise of the quantum-geometric shift current of exciton polaritons can measure photon-number statistics and, for pure states, infer the QFI. By solving the Lindblad equation, we obtain the time-dependent nonlinear photocurrent for an arbitrary initial photon state. It turns out that, regardless of the quantum state of the incident light, the integrated current depends only on the mean photon number. In contrast, the shot noise retains information about photon-number fluctuations: Its Fano factor is proportional to the photon-number variance. Numerical calculations confirm these relations for optical Schrödinger cat and squeezed-vacuum states. A photodetector based on shift current noise can therefore provide a solid-state platform for high-precision measurements of quantum-optical statistics without relying on mobile photocarriers.

items.title: Reproducibility of social science research using aggregate statistics with noise infused for differential privacy
items.summary_raw: Privacy-preserving analytics such as differential privacy are designed to allow the analysis of sensitive datasets while protecting individuals’ privacy. Their deployment, however, has been controversial. Critics maintain that statistical noise injected to preserve privacy can degrade the quality and feasibility of social science research. We select a benchmark of empirical findings from 93 published social science studies involving regression analyses over aggregate statistics. We evaluate whether their findings replicate on privacy noise-infused data. Under privacy budgets typical in industry, around 91% of simulated findings still support the original claims at significance level α = 0.1 . Claims based on weaker original effect sizes are more likely to be nullified or sometimes reversed. We compare distortions caused by privacy noise to those due to measurement errors and other kinds of nonsampling errors common in social statistics, and we find that the marginal impacts of privacy protection are smaller. Moreover, discrepancies due to privacy noise are often much smaller than discrepancies observed in traditional replication and robustness studies.

items.title: IGF2BP1 in 17q-gain cooperates with MYCN to regulate purine biosynthesis and immunotherapy efficacy in neuroblastoma
items.summary_raw: Concurrent chromosomal 17q-gain and MYCN amplification define a subset of neuroblastoma associated with particularly adverse clinical outcomes. However, how these genetic alterations synergize to promote tumor progression and whether their cooperation confers therapeutic vulnerabilities remain elusive. We herein performed a CRISPR-based functional screen targeting 17q-gain genes and identified the RNA m 6 A reader IGF2BP1 as a critical MYCN collaborator to promote aggressive neuroblastomas via activation of phosphoribosylaminoimidazole succinocarboxamide synthetase (PAICS), a key enzyme involved in de novo purine biosynthesis. Rewiring of PAICS-mediated nucleotide metabolism enabled tumor cells to sustain necessary purine pools for productive transcription of replicative stress-responsive genes, including CHK1 , to cope with the exacerbated replication stress. Pharmacological inhibition of CHK1 elicited a robust immune reprogramming, leading to activation of cGAS–STING signaling, upregulation of Major Histocompatibility Complex class I expression, and synergistic tumor suppression with immune checkpoint blockade. Altogether, we identify an IGF2BP1/MYCN–PAICS–CHK1 axis that drives aggressive neuroblastoma phenotypes and constitutes an actionable vulnerability for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: A second-generation “hypoxia in a pill” rescues neurodegenerative phenotypes across distinct mouse models
items.summary_raw: A growing body of preclinical research is demonstrating the therapeutic potential of chronic, continuous hypoxia (11% FIO 2 ) for rare and common diseases. However, the chronic delivery of hypoxic gas poses both practical challenges and long-term safety concerns. We previously introduced a small-molecule, “hypoxia-in-a-pill” combining a hemoglobin affinity enhancer (GBT440) to limit oxygen delivery with a HIF-2α inhibitor (PT2399) to prevent detrimental compensatory erythropoiesis. Although this small-molecule regimen extended the lifespan of the Ndufs4 knockout (KO) mouse model of mitochondrial complex I deficiency and Leigh syndrome, its efficacy did not match chronic 11% FIO 2 . Here we optimize this regimen using GBT601, a second-generation hemoglobin affinity enhancer with longer half-life and greater hemoglobin occupancy, and show it rescues key neurodegenerative phenotypes in multiple models. When we initiate therapy in 50 d old Ndufs4 KO mice with advanced disease, GBT601 monotherapy alleviated neurological disease phenotypes and extended median lifespan from 62 to 105 d, while dual therapy with the GBT601/PT2399 combination extended median lifespan to 158 d. When initiated after onset of advanced disease in a mouse model of Friedreich’s ataxia, the combination halted further progression of motor phenotypes. items.title: SETDB1 preferentially silences evolutionarily young retroelements
items.summary_raw: Transposable elements (TEs) are epigenetically silenced through multiple mechanisms, including heterochromatin formation and DNA methylation. Prior studies have implicated SETDB1 and the Human Silencing Hub (HUSH) complex in heterochromatin formation-based TE repression, but precise characterization of repeat subclass and locus-specific effects for SETDB1 and related mechanisms has been limited by short-read transcriptome mapping. Here, we use long-read RNA sequencing mapped to a telomere-to-telomere mouse genome assembly to resolve the specific contributions of SETDB1 to TE silencing at single-locus resolution. Knockdown of SETDB1 or core HUSH factors reveals robust and reproducible derepression of a restricted subset of long terminal repeat (LTR) retroelements distinct from those of global DNA demethylation. This derepression is heterogeneous within TE subclasses and is confined to discrete genomic loci, highlighting regulatory diversity that is obscured by aggregate, family-level analyses. Time-resolved SETDB1 depletion followed by histone 3 lysine 9 (H3K9)me3, H3K9me2, and Pol II ChIP-seq reveals a stratified derepression response: ERVK and ERV1 elements show concordant H3K9 methylation loss, Pol II gain, and RNA expression induction, consistent with direct H3K9me3-mediated silencing, whereas LINE/L1 elements show transcriptional activation without corresponding H3K9me3 loss, implicating parallel repressive mechanisms. items.title: Pity the Next Insurance Commissioner of Oklahoma
items.summary_raw: In the waning weeks of the midterm election cycle, the question of who will serve as Oklahoma’s next insurance commissioner is unlikely to be a topic of intense speculation at dinner tables around the country — or in Oklahoma, for that matter. For one thing, it’s about as down-ballot a race as you can get, another bubble to be filled in alongside state treasurer and superintendent of public instruction. For another, it’s difficult to imagine it will be much of a competition: It’s been two decades since a Democrat last won statewide office in Oklahoma. But if there ever were a race for an upset, this would be it. Oklahoma is one of the most expensive places in the country to purchase home insurance, with an average annual premium in 2024 of over $5,819 for $350,000 in dwelling coverage — well above the national average of $3,303 and behind only Florida and Louisiana, per the most recent numbers from the Consumer Federation of America. That’s even more staggering given the local cost of living: Oklahomans spend more of their median household income , $65,039, than residents in any other state on home insurance — almost 9%. When it comes to arguing for greater industry regulation, Democrats are typically on more comfortable footing against their conservative counterparts. Craig MacIntyre, the Democrat in the Oklahoma insurance commissioner race, has promised to use the state’s new “file and wait” law to review rate increase requests closely before they’re implemented. items.title: The Louisiana wind industry’s plan for survival: Outlast Trump
items.summary_raw: Louisiana’s offshore wind industry has a date circled on the calendar: January 21, 2029 — the first day after President Donald Trump is scheduled to leave office. Trump’s policies have brought offshore wind development to a near standstill around the country, with his administration paying developers roughly $4 billion to walk away from projects. But in Louisiana, leaders in the industry say they are trying to preserve their expertise and supply chain in hopes of reviving offshore wind projects under the next administration. “Come January 21st, 2029, we all get to wave goodbye,” said state Representative Joe Orgeron, a Republican from southeastern Louisiana who worked in the offshore wind industry. “The current administration has been a one-man stopping show. I’m pretty confident, and I’m hopeful that it’ll change.” Orgeron later put the industry’s near-term strategy more succinctly: “Just wait for the clock to run out.” His views were echoed by the other wind energy experts on a panel at Tulane University’s Future of Energy Forum . “The Trump administration has been pretty openly hostile to seeing the advancement of the offshore wind industry,” said Madelyn Smith, a program manager with the Southeastern Wind Coalition, a nonprofit that supports the development of wind power across 11 states. items.title: ‘Digger’ has a lot of haters. Here’s why they’re wrong.
items.summary_raw: Last week, this magazine published a review of Digger , the new climate change allegory from Mexican provocateur Alejandro Iñárritu. In it, my colleague Jake Bittle explains in detail why he “ hated it .” I was skeptical of the bad reviews that Digger has been getting; after all, I like more of the Iñárritu films I’ve seen than not. I would even call one of them (his 2001 debut, Amores Perros ) a cinematic masterpiece. ( Birdman was fine.) In any case, most of the time a Mexican person is in the news, I am invested in their success, so I decided to see the movie for myself. Even then — two hours, nine minutes, and a small popcorn later — I was surprised by my reaction: I simply loved the movie. Despite the negative reviews and poor box-office numbers, Digger is a film well-worth seeing — and talking about. To do that fully, this review contains spoilers. Digger is Iñárritu’s most ambitious, visually maximalist, thematically convoluted, and sonically grating movie yet. Or as Jake puts it, yes, it is “ugly, loud, and unpleasant,” but I didn’t mind the sensory overload. In fact, it’s part of why I liked it. There are plenty of movies that try to capture the non-stop roar of the so-called unprecedented times we live in: Sorry to Bother You, Uncut Gems , and Eddington come to mind. These movies offer up cacophony as a form of contemporary social commentary. They’re grating on purpose, because that’s often how waking up, checking your phone, and heading to work feels. Digger joins…

items.summary_raw: Spotřebitelé čelí výzvám k úhradě údajných starších dluhů jan.hamrnik@er… Pá, 10/09/2026 - 09:29 Na Energetický regulační úřad (ERÚ) se v posledních dnech obracejí spotřebitelé se stížností na totožnou praktiku. Advokátní kancelář je vyzývá k zaplacení údajného letitého dluhu, který mají mít u bývalého dodavatele. Dokument je formulován jako předžalobní výzva, neobsahuje žádné podklady a často ani nespecifikuje, z čeho by pohledávka měla plynout. ERÚ zákazníkům radí, jak postupovat. Rozhodně by neměli domnělý dluh automaticky platit! „Na základě neuhrazeného vyúčtování u společnosti (…) Vám vznikla vůči této společnosti dlužná pohledávka ve výši XY,“ stojí ve výzvě, kvůli níž se na ERÚ během posledních dní obrátilo několik spotřebitelů. Advokátní kancelář v ní zastupuje klienta vymáhajícího pohledávky od dodavatelů, kteří již několik let nepůsobí na trhu. Regulátor doposud narazil na údajně neuhrazené částky společnostem Lidová energie a ELGAS Energy, na něž v době jejich působnosti na trhu registroval velké množství stížností, a jimž dokonce zrušil licence na obchod s elektřinou i plynem. „Spotřebitelé by určitě neměli domnělý starší dluh automaticky uhradit pouze na základě doručené výzvy. items.title: Permitting Reform’s Battle Lines Are Taking Shape
items.summary_raw: This is Heatmap Daily, an evening digest written by our executive editor. It’s now been just over a week since a gang of four bipartisan senators released the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA. The permitting reform proposal would make too many changes to federal law to summarize cleanly here — read our explainer for that — but suffice it to say it creates a messy group of winners and losers. Utilities, data centers, and the Trump administration would lose; electricity ratepayers, clean energy companies, long-distance transmission lines, and natural gas pipeline builders win. (As would geothermal startups, virtual power plant providers, and a few other climate tech subsectors that my colleague Katie Brigham recently detailed .) In the ensuing week since its release, we’ve gotten a better sense of the battle lines over the bill. The hardhat unions largely support the proposal (although the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, which is often aligned with utility executives, has stayed notably silent on it.) Clean energy trade groups, such as the American Clean Power Association, back it, too, as do fossil fuel lobbying groups, such as the American Petroleum Institute. Groups representing the environmental and climate movement are more split, and some of the most influential nonprofits have yet to render a verdict. Earlier today, the Sierra Club published its first take on the proposal, which it described as a “hard look” at the bill. The…

items.title: Disability inclusion for just transitions: A semi-systematic review of representations of persons with disabilities in energy transition research
Market waste composition, biomethane yield, and energy potential in Nairobi, Kenya
items.summary_raw: Introduction: Municipal solid waste (MSW) management remains a critical sustainability challenge in rapidly urbanizing cities, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa where inadequate infrastructure and reliance on unsanitary landfills exacerbate greenhouse gas emissions. Nairobi, Kenya, generates approximately 3600 tons of MSW daily, with up to 40% uncollected, straining the only dumpsite at Dandora. Material and methods: This study investigated the biomethane potential of waste from 23 food markets, applying standardized compositional analysis and anaerobic digestion (AD) protocols. Results: Results show that market waste is predominantly organic (67%), with significant variability in moisture content, volatile solids (VS) and total solids (TS). The City market exhibited the highest biomethane potentials (76.27 m 3 /ton), while En recorded the lowest values (36.51 m 3 /ton). Inferential statistics confirmed significant heterogeneity across markets (Kruskal–Wallis, p < 0.001), with regression analysis explaining 97.4% of yield variance. The final regression model identified moisture content as the strongest negative predictor (β = 0.883, p < 0.001). Collectively, the 289 tons of organic market waste produced daily could generate ~14,230 m 3 of biomethane, equivalent to 137,000 kWh of energy. Conclusions: These findings highlight AD as a viable waste-to-energy pathway, offering renewable energy generation, climate mitigation, and employment opportunities. Policy recommendations…

items.title: What is energy literacy? From prerequisite for participation to social practice
items.summary_raw: Energy literacy is often assumed to be a prerequisite for public participation in energy. But, it remains unclear how people's energy literacy leads to participation. This raises questions about dominant conceptualisations of energy literacy in relation to participation. We investigated energy literacy in relation to participation in energy communities, which are seen as important contexts for stimulating both. Following an abductive approach, we synthesized insights from diverse bodies of literature with empirical data from Greek energy communities, drawing on interviews and focus groups with 20 participants from energy community core teams and supporting organizations. We developed two perspectives on energy literacy, each assuming a different relation between energy literacy and participation, leading to different approaches for stimulating both. The first perspective sees energy literacy as a prerequisite for participation. It treats energy literacy as static ability that people have or lack, and operationalizes it through standardized, prescriptive, and isolated approaches. This view overlooks people's diverse needs. Therefore, we developed a broader view of energy literacy as social practice, that conceptualises energy literacy as something people do in their specific situation. Energy literacy and participation are intertwined, and operationalized through contextualized, dynamic, diverse and tailored approaches. Although the two perspectives depart from distinct…

items.title: Learning from young conservatives: Increasing pro-environmental behavior change and climate policy support in the United States
items.summary_raw: This study uses a mixed-methods (i.e., virtual focus groups with group discussion based on live polling results) approach to explore which potential interventions show the most promise for engaging conservatives on the topics of climate policy and household action, specifically among young people in the United States (U.S.). In coordination with the non-profit organization American Conservation Coalition (ACC), we held six virtual focus groups with ACC members from geographically diverse chapters. Using our mixed methods approach, we explored political efficacy, as suggested by ACC members, as well as four messaging types informed by the social psychological literature: superordinate identities, solution aversion, pluralistic ignorance, and personal responsibility. Our results suggest that young conservative study participants identified messages intended to address solution aversion and pluralistic ignorance to be most promising. Our results also suggest that although young conservative participants in the study tend to engage in incremental, convenient pro-environmental behaviors, they are optimistic about the potential for positive spillover effects. Additionally, our focus groups revealed that a promising area of future study is that young conservatives could serve as important messengers for pro-environmental individual action and support for climate and energy policies among their conservative peers. Thus, the study suggests promising topics for research on the role…

items.title: The embeddedness of Emissions Trading Systems
Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China
items.summary_raw: The increasing trend in CO 2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO 2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing of raw biomass is a promising carbon–neutral energy option in China, but its application is limited to only 10% incorporation with stable combustion performance. Therefore, in this study comprehensively assessed biomass upgrading methods, including torrefaction, pelletization, pyrolysis, and gasification, demonstrated that upgraded biomass exhibited significant potential as an attractive, feasible, and sustainable alternative fuel for a low-carbon approach to co-firing in existing PC power plants. The existing research work revealed that the recent Chinese energy policies support the co-firing of biomass, while biomass upgrading technologies are under development and need bioenergy-supported policies. The results showed that upgraded biomass enables higher co-firing ratios in PC boilers, achieving up to 50% substitution on an energy basis and reducing net CO 2 emissions by up to 50% compared with full coal combustion. Co-firing of the upgraded biomass not only maintains the high efficiency of PC and CFB furnaces, but also has the potential to lower their carbon footprint and NO x emissions. Additionally, the effectiveness of the co-firing strategy for achieving carbon neutrality is evaluated. This review paper can assist in identifying the…

items.title: Climate governance as care: Towards an Indigenous Environmental Justice approach
items.summary_raw: Within international climate governance, anthropogenic climate change is predominantly framed through the lens of harm. While this framing has been instrumental in advancing mitigation, adaptation and accountability mechanisms, it remains limited in its capacity to capture the structural, relational and historically embedded nature of the climate crisis. Drawing on insights from urban political ecology (UPE) and Indigenous Environmental Justice (IEJ), this article argues that dominant approaches to climate governance rely on forms of abstraction that render complex socio-ecological relations governable while obscuring the colonial, capitalist and uneven processes through which climate change is produced and experienced. In particular, prevailing legal frameworks privilege calculable harms, individualised responsibility and market-based solutions, marginalising the slow, cumulative and differentiated forms of environmental violence that shape lived realities. To address these limitations, the article reorients climate governance scholarship towards a care-centred perspective. It examines how a focus on care challenges the epistemological foundations of mainstream climate justice, including the construction of ‘climate harms’, ‘climate subjects’ and ‘climate solutions’. By foregrounding interdependence, reciprocity and responsibility, care offers an alternative framework for understanding climate change as a crisis of disrupted socio-ecological relations rather than discrete…

items.title: Public Attitudes and Legal Ambiguity: Results From a Survey on Medical Cannabis in Slovenia
items.summary_raw: Public attitudes toward medical cannabis play an important role in shaping regulatory practice and integrating new therapies into health systems. This online survey of Slovenian adults (n = 226) examined perceptions of medical cannabis within a context of legal ambiguity and limited institutional guidance. Support for legalization was high, but respondents commonly reported unclear understanding of what current law permits and limited trust in the accuracy of information received from healthcare professionals. Participants relied heavily on informal and online sources, highlighting gaps in regulatory clarity and professional readiness. These findings underscore the need for clear legal frameworks, improved clinical guidance, and more transparent communication to align public expectations with medical and legal practice in Slovenia.

items.title: Environmental Advocacy and Visual Framing: Social Documentary Filmmaking as a Tool for Legitimation and Change
items.summary_raw: This study examines the impact of narrative technologies on the perception of environmental advocacy. The aim is to evaluate how the social documentary “Brazil: Seeding Sociobioeconomies” acts as a strategic device for communication and social mobilization. The research question investigates how visual narrative strategies and compositional structuring deconstruct traditional framings of the climate crisis, reimagining the relationship between biocultural memory, innovation, and sustainable development. The methodology is based on the conceptual distinction between narration and storytelling, applying the method of Visual Narrative Analysis (VNA) to interpret the translation of discourse into moving images and its capacity to construct social reality, complemented by Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) and, more specifically, its multimodal evolution, Multimodal Critical Discourse Analysis (MCDA). The expected results aim to demonstrate that social documentary works as a legitimizing tool, accrediting the socio-bioeconomy not as a nostalgic regression, but rather as an updating of memory and an evolution of identity capable of guaranteeing sustainability and global climate justice.

items.title: A hot agenda? Climate change and international student mobility: a scoping review of the literature
items.source_name: British Journal of Sociology of Education
items.summary_raw: International student mobility (ISM) has become central to higher education, yet its relationship with climate change remains insufficiently researched. This paper argues that existing scholarship concentrates on two limited approaches, quantifying student travel emissions and celebrating ISM as fostering climate awareness, whilst reproducing analytical blind spots characterising mainstream ISM research for decades. Both ainadequately address social inequalities and colonial legacies, while neglecting how climate change itself may be reshaping ISM patterns. We propose a research agenda centred on two priorities: (1) adopting intersectional analysis to examine how multiple inequalities shape students’ differentiated relationships to climate change, and (2) integrating decolonial perspectives that challenge Northern epistemic dominance and reposition Global South students as knowledge producers. Pursued alongside engagement with climate mobilities scholarship, this reorientation positions equity at the centre of ISM-climate research, moving beyond reductive framings toward understanding educational mobility within systems of inequality and ­environmental transformation.

items.title: The multidimensionality of green transition attitudes and their role in sustainable mobility uptake
items.summary_raw: Although sustainable mobility is a key societal target, understanding the local determinants of individual transport mode choice amidst decarbonization remains underdeveloped. This study addresses this gap and explores how the multidimensionality of green transition attitudes influences sustainable mobility uptake in Italy. We find four key components of green transition attitudes: the respondents’ attitudes toward (1) performance of actors and institutions in green transition and ensuring its fairness, (2) policies to limit climate change in a way that is inclusive and fair and leaves no one behind, (3) contributing to the green transition through jobs, skills, and personal responsibility beyond the workplace, and (4) taking action to fight climate change. Our findings demonstrate that positive assessments of actors and institutions’ performance and fairness in managing the green transition are significantly linked to a higher likelihood of choosing walking over using private motorized vehicles, suggesting that individuals who hold favorable views of sustainability-promoting actors and institutions are more receptive to utilizing sustainable transport modes and supporting evidence that trust and perceived legitimacy are pivotal in fostering pro-environmental choices. These results offer valuable guidance for promoting greener transport solutions and advancing the sustainable mobility agenda that is inclusive, evidence-based, and context-specific.

items.title: Synergistic impacts of low-carbon city pilot policy and information consumption pilot policy on carbon lock-in
items.summary_raw: Introduction Carbon lock-in poses a significant barrier to the low-carbon transition, necessitating synergistic policy interventions. Methods Using a dual machine learning (DML) model, this study estimates carbon lock-in data for 262 Chinese cities and examines how the dual policy (the low-carbon city pilot and information consumption pilot policy) affects carbon lock-in. Results The dual policy significantly suppresses carbon lock-in, with a markedly stronger effect than implementing either policy in isolation. The analysis indicates that the dual policy works through industrial structure upgrading, government environmental support, climate technology innovation, and public climate concern. Additionally, the heterogeneity test reveals that the suppressive effect is more pronounced in non-resource-based cities, large cities, and those with high market vitality and strong financial regulation. Discussion Consequently, this study provides evidence for promoting the synergistic implementation of the low-carbon city pilot and the information consumption pilot policy, thereby breaking carbon lock-in.

items.title: Contracting as Sensemaking Infrastructure: Enacting Sustainability Strategy in Business‐to‐Business Relationships
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Firms articulate sustainability objectives but depend on suppliers and business partners to enact them. As commitments cross organizational and professional boundaries, their meaning may fragment even when parties agree in principle. This theory‐synthesis article examines B2B contracting as sensemaking infrastructure for enacting sustainability strategy across interorganizational relationships. Integrating sensemaking, proactive contracting, and contract design, it develops the sensemaking‐based contracting framework. The framework identifies four interdependent functions: framing clarifies what the relationship seeks to govern; translation connects that understanding to responsibilities, data, and routines; adaptation organizes legitimate revision; and signaling connects relationship‐level performance to external credibility. The article repositions contracting from downstream compliance to strategy enactment. It shows that preserving contractual wording is insufficient when purpose becomes disconnected from performance and directs managerial attention to connections among purpose, responsibility, capability, review, and evidence. Whether this infrastructure supports shared meaning depends on power, network position, and actors' ability to question established interpretations.

items.title: Congratulatory messages on the publication of this guidance
Beyond production: understanding aquaculture narratives, public engagement, and visibility on TikTok and Instagram
items.summary_raw: Public acceptance and societal trust are increasingly recognized as critical challenges for sustainable aquaculture development. While previous research has examined consumer perceptions and social acceptance, limited attention has been given to how aquaculture narratives are constructed, circulated, and gain visibility within contemporary digital media environments. This study examines how thematic patterns, sentiment, audience engagement, and narrative construction shape aquaculture communication on TikTok and Instagram. Using a mixed-method approach integrating computational analysis, machine learning, and qualitative framing analysis, aquaculture-related posts were examined to understand patterns of representation, interaction, and narrative visibility. Industry and Production content represented the most prevalent thematic category but did not consistently generate the highest audience engagement, indicating that visibility was not determined by content prevalence alone. Although represented by only a small number of posts, Animal Welfare content showed comparatively high engagement; this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Qualitative framing analysis revealed that highly visible aquaculture content extended beyond technical production narratives, positioning the sector through broader frames related to sustainability solutions, transparency, innovation, livelihoods, commercial opportunities, and societal concerns. The findings demonstrate that digital…

items.title: Do government subsidy policies promote the energy transition resilience of enterprises? Empirical evidence from China
items.source_name: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
items.summary_raw: Purpose Energy transition resilience (ETR) captures enterprises’ capacity to maintain sustainability during low-carbon transitions. This paper aims to construct a comprehensive ETR evaluation index system and examines how government subsidies affect enterprises’ ETR. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from 2013 to 2023 on small and medium-sized enterprises listed on China’s A-share SME and ChiNext boards to construct a comprehensive ETR evaluation index system. Econometric models are used to empirically test the impact of government subsidies on enterprises’ ETR, while further analysing the mediating role of financing constraints, the threshold moderating effect of environmental regulations and heterogeneity across ownership, region and industry. Findings The results indicate that: government subsidies significantly enhance enterprises’ ETR; the resource-based and signalling functions of government subsidies improve ETR by easing financing constraints; environmental regulations exert a countervailing moderating effect on the relationship between government subsidies and ETR, displaying a single threshold; and government subsidies have a stronger positive effect on ETR among non-state-owned enterprises, eastern enterprises and manufacturing enterprises. Practical implications The findings offer empirical support for governments to optimise subsidy policies and improve environmental regulation systems. They also provide decision-making references for…

items.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Biomethane Market Integration in Ukraine: Feedstocks, Infrastructure, and Decarbonisation
items.summary_raw: Biomethane production from agricultural residues and livestock waste offers Ukraine a strategic pathway to strengthen energy security, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and integrate renewable gases into the European energy system. This study develops and evaluates three scenarios for the Ukrainian biomethane market under European integration: conservative, baseline, and innovation-driven integration. The scenarios differ in investment intensity, public support, regulatory alignment with EU requirements, deployment of anaerobic digestion and biogas upgrading technologies, sustainability certification, and access to domestic and cross-border gas infrastructure. An integrated scenario framework combines agricultural feedstock availability, technological readiness, institutional conditions, market integration, and environmental effects. The results indicate that Ukraine has substantial potential to become an important producer and supplier of sustainable biomethane to the European Union because of its large agricultural resource base, existing gas infrastructure, and geographical proximity to EU markets (projected production in 2030 of 0.26–0.88 billion m3/year, required capital expenditure ranging from EUR 360 million to EUR 1.51 billion, and emission reductions ranging from 443.6 to 649.8 thousand t CO2-eq/year under the conservative scenario, from 870.2 to 1274.6 thousand t CO2-eq/year under the baseline scenario, and from 1464.1 to 2144.6 thousand t CO2-eq/year under the…

items.title: Developmentalism without a developmental state: Fragmented capacities and green hydrogen in Chile
items.summary_raw: How do states with limited economic resources pursue ambitious green industrial transitions when their outcomes remain uncertain? This article examines this question through Chile's green hydrogen strategy in Patagonia, where ministries, regional governments, state-owned enterprises, and CORFO must coordinate within a predominantly neoliberal political economy. Drawing on 27 sequential qualitative interviews with state actors and lay participants, alongside documentary analysis, we show that the transition is assembled through uneven capacities rather than a unified developmental apparatus. First, regional actors build a green development project by translating global decarbonization into a locally grounded agenda and assembling the infrastructure, skills, partnerships, and other enabling conditions required for private investment, despite constrained fiscal resources and legislative authority. Second, the “hyper-sectoral” organization of the Chilean state makes coordination a central developmental task: strategic, regulatory, fiscal, and administrative capacities sit in different organizations, while regional governments use relational, discursive, and performative power to mobilize actors they cannot command. Third, development is also a matter of governing expectations. Official promises encourage residents to invest in education and occupations linked to anticipated jobs, even as uncertainty persists over whether projects will materialize and who will benefit. Taken…

items.title: Topographic variation shapes organismal responses across mountain landscapes
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02773-z The authors developed simulations to examine the role of topographic variation in mediating species response to climate change. They show that topographic variation can reduce energy expenditure by up to 20.8% and increase buffering benefits of elevation shifts by 82.1% for a diurnal ectotherm.

items.title: Farmers’ knowledge, attitudes and perceptions of green hydrogen in Oshikoto Region, Namibia
items.summary_raw: Introduction: Commercial farmers in Namibia’s Oshikoto Region operate under drought, water scarcity, high agricultural input costs and uneven rural energy access. Although Namibia has prioritised green hydrogen within its industrial and energy strategies, limited farmer-level evidence explains how potential agricultural applications are understood and evaluated. Materials and methods: The study adopted an exploratory qualitative design grounded in interpretivism. Ten commercial farmers were recruited purposively, supplemented by convenience access and snowball referrals. Semi-structured interviews with video-assisted elicitation examined knowledge, attitudes and perceptions of green hydrogen, green ammonia and hydrogen-supported agricultural energy systems. The data were examined through deductive and inductive thematic analysis. Saturation was assessed through interview-by-interview comparison of codes and analytical memoranda. Results: Baseline responses showed limited operational knowledge of electrolysis, hydrogen storage, green ammonia production, irrigation-energy systems and associated safety requirements. Comparison of pre-video and post-video responses showed that the educational video increased the specificity of participants’ evaluations: participants became better able to identify possible agricultural applications and anticipated benefits. However, cross-participant comparison revealed substantial conditionality. Expected benefits relating to fertiliser costs…

items.title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
items.summary_raw: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. Our research applied a value-based approach to understand how place attachment and the perceived community impacts of policy interventions influence coastal residents’ support for different MSP options that vary in emphasis between economic exploitation and nature protection. We engaged with residents around Dundalk Bay, Ireland, using a survey which presented two evidence-based MSP options (describing the status quo implying a moderate Marine Protected Area [MPA] co-existing with economic activities, versus a highly protected MPA) in randomised order. We captured participants’ personal values, economic and natural place attachment (EPA; NPA), and the perceived community impacts of each MSP option. We conducted regression analyses and a parallel-serial mediation analysis to determine each factor’s direct and indirect effects on MSP support. Most respondents preferred a shift towards stronger nature protection in the bay. Our analysis supports a multidimensional approach to place attachment and indicates that the alignment of biospheric values, NPA, and perceived community impacts is important for MSP option choice. This is less the case for EPA and its…

items.title: Staging the burden of the now: What participatory theatre reveals about the limits of a just transition in South Africa
Morality and climate policy attitudes
items.summary_raw: This paper studies the moral roots of climate policy attitudes. We fielded a survey with a representative sample in the US to study the predictive power of moral universalism in explaining heterogeneity in specific climate policy attitudes. Our results reveal that universalism is significantly related to support for various policy measures that prevail in current policy debates in most countries, including domestic policies such as a carbon tax and a green infrastructure program, as well as international policies such as international burden-sharing. Supporting evidence comes from simple bystander allocation decisions in which respondents are asked to decide “who should pay” to fight climate change or to mitigate the adverse consequences of global warming. Open-text elicitations further corroborate these results and identify moral universalism as a key aspect of how people reason about climate policies.

items.title: Reviewing the climate change landscape in South Africa’s marine fisheries: progress, gaps, and future directions
items.summary_raw: Climate change is reshaping South Africa’s marine ecosystems and fisheries with consequences for ecological productivity, livelihoods and governance. Although research on climate impacts on fisheries has expanded, the overall climate-risk landscape for South African fisheries has not been reviewed using the risk framing proposed in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). Drawing on 72 peer-reviewed publications (between 1996 and July 2023) together with targeted grey literature, and applying explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, this paper examines how previously published climate change research in the South African marine system addresses the AR5 risk-based components (hazard, exposure, vulnerability) and the associated response dimension of adaptation across ecological, social and social-ecological domains. The review shows strong evidence for ecological change but far less integration of social and governance dimensions that shape real-world risk and adaptive capacity. Most studies focus on vulnerability and impacts, with limited explicit characterisation of climate hazards, spatial exposure or full risk assessments. Research effort is geographically uneven, concentrated in the southern Benguela, and adaptation planning remains fragmented across institutions. Collectively, these patterns indicate that South Africa has substantial knowledge of climate impacts but lacks the coordinated frameworks required to operationalise…

items.title: Older Adults’ Meaning-Making of Climate Change and Their Perceived Capacity for Action: A Qualitative Study
items.summary_raw: Objective: This study explored how community-dwelling older adults construct, interpret, and respond to climate change in their everyday lives, how they emotionally position themselves in relation to climate change, and how they perceive their capacity for action toward climate change.Materials and Methods: A qualitative design was employed. In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with community-dwelling older adults in İzmir using purposive sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed through inductive thematic analysis. Credibility was supported through data saturation and participant checking.Results: Four interrelated themes were identified: (a) understanding climate change, (b) future perceptions and intergenerational assessments, (c) experiencing climate events and coping processes, and (d) individual responsibility and adaptation practices. Climate change was primarily constructed through observable environmental changes, particularly heat and drought, and frequently framed as a future-oriented and intergenerational concern. Participants described emotional responses, including worry and anxiety, alongside embodied and daily-life impacts of climate events. Adaptation practices were largely household-based and conservation-oriented, motivated by responsibility toward society and future generations. Despite strong ethical concern, perceived structural agency remained limited.Conclusion: Findings suggest that climate change in…

items.title: Climate policies and adaptive capacities: a cross-analysis of sectoral, intersectoral, and international actions
items.summary_raw: Against intensifying climate risks, this study compares the associations of sectoral, cross-sectoral, and international climate policies with annual changes in adaptation readiness. Using an unbalanced panel of 59 countries from 2002 to 2022, it estimates OLS and SUR models with policy–income interactions and assesses robustness through Mundlak and dynamic GMM specifications. Cross-sectoral policies display the most consistent positive association with readiness improvements, although Wald tests show no statistically significant difference between their coefficients and those of sectoral policies. The two approaches therefore appear complementary rather than substitutable. International policies are mainly associated with improvements in lower-income countries, and their contribution weakens as income rises. The findings emphasize cross-sectoral coordination, sector-specific expertise, sustained implementation, and strategies adapted to national economic and institutional capacities.

items.title: Justice Coherence in Climate Legislation: A Design‐Level Evaluation of South Africa's Climate Change Act 22 of 2024
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT South Africa's Climate Change Act 22 of 2024 was enacted amid escalating climate risk, entrenched inequality, carbon‐intensive development, and uneven state capacity. This article evaluates the Act at the level of policy design rather than implementation outcomes. Gilbert and Terrell's allocation, provision, delivery, and finance dimensions are combined with distributive, procedural, recognitional, and restorative climate‐justice criteria. The Act and its commencement proclamation were coded at section and subsection level using a transparent matrix classifying justice mechanisms as present, partial, or absent. The analysis identifies four recurring design gaps: recognition without binding priority, participation without guaranteed influence, implementation mandates without differentiated capacity support, and justice commitments without fully specified finance or restorative mechanisms. Comparative reference to framework climate legislation in the United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand, and Victoria shows that these challenges are not unique to South Africa. The article advances the concept of justice coherence, arguing that climate justice should be traced across the full policy‐design chain. The framework provides a transferable basis for comparative analysis of climate legislation while remaining sensitive to jurisdiction‐specific institutions, capacities, and different implementation conditions.

items.title: The bipartisan energy bill tearing the climate movement apart
items.summary_raw: In order to solve climate change, you have to do two things — stop burning fossil fuels, and build clean energy to replace them. The last few decades in the United States have witnessed a long back-and-forth over which of the two goals is more important, and over how to achieve either of them. Is it more important to pass a carbon tax, or subsidize electric vehicles? To block a new oil pipeline, or build a lot of solar and wind? On this question, the coalition known as the climate movement has fractured into two broad groups. On one side, there are activists, lawyers, and environmentalists, who tend to focus on blocking and reducing fossil fuel use. On the other, there are renewable energy companies and policy wonks, who tend to focus on building more clean energy. These factions have clashed in the past, but over the past week a kind of civil war has erupted between the different elements of the climate movement. The inciting incident was the release of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, a long-awaited Senate bill that is designed to enable the construction of more power plants, transmission lines, and gas pipelines. The bill does this by weakening some of the nation’s bedrock environmental laws, speeding up the timeline for government agencies to issue permits, and making it harder to cancel projects that have already gotten federal approval. For climate-conscious supporters of the bill, it’s better for the planet to build a lot of clean energy…

items.title: Hurricane Isaias is a typical storm — but it’s also ‘astounding’
items.summary_raw: Something strange just popped up in the Gulf of Mexico: a hurricane. Well, not so much Hurricane Isaias, which strengthened into a Category 3 before its predicted landfall along the Florida Panhandle late Friday. It’s more the timing of it: This is the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, which began all the way back in June. That smashes the previous record in the satellite era for the latest first hurricane of a season, September 11. “This is pretty astounding, really, to break a record by just about a month,” said Brian McNoldy, a senior research associate who studies hurricanes at the University of Miami. So what’s with the extraordinary delay? El Niño, of all things . Even though that band of warm water is on the other side of the Americas in the Pacific, it messes with two of the fundamental ingredients for making hurricanes in the Atlantic: wind and humidity. To spawn a tropical cyclone, you need warm water, which provides energy, as well as high humidity and winds moving in a consistent direction. (Hurricanes have been getting more intense lately because climate change is rapidly warming the oceans , creating high-octane fuel.) While the Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico have been plenty warm, providing huge pools of fuel, El Niño has been messing with weather patterns, creating dry, sinking air. It also provides wind shear — air moving at different directions and speeds as you gain altitude — which hurricanes really hate. Hence the exceptionally quiet Atlantic…
