items.title: Large language models unlock the ecology of species interactions
items.summary_raw: Species interactions shape population dynamics, geographic distributions, evolutionary trajectories, and responses to environmental change. Yet data on these interactions remain scarce across broad spatial, temporal, and taxonomic scales because they are difficult to collect in the field. One promising source of interaction data is citizen science platforms, which contain billions of biodiversity observations, often accompanied by unstructured text comments that may document interactions among organisms. Advances in large language models (LLMs) make it increasingly feasible to identify, extract, and categorize biotic interactions from these unstructured data at scale. Here, we present an LLM workflow that collects species interaction observations from multilingual citizen science comments. Using two case studies—bird–bird and plant–pollinator interactions—we show that LLMs can rapidly extract interaction types and participating species with high accuracy. These data can greatly expand the spatial, temporal, and taxonomic coverage and resolution of species interactions data, enable new tests of long-standing ecological questions, and improve our ability to track ecological changes. With appropriate validation, expert review, and attention to data privacy for both users and sensitive species, this approach opens new opportunities to characterize, forecast, and conserve biodiversity under global change.

items.title: Mechanotherapy enhances nanodrug uptake by overcoming the actin cytoskeleton damping effect
items.summary_raw: Efficient nanodrug therapy in solid tumors is limited not only by extracellular barriers but also by the mechanical state of the plasma membrane (PM). Although mechanotherapy remodels the extracellular matrix (ECM) and improves tissue-level delivery, its effect on transmembrane transport remains unclear. Here, we show that matrix stiffness is transmitted to the PM through the actomyosin cytoskeleton and thereby regulates nanoparticle (NP) uptake. Within a hepatocellular carcinoma-relevant stiffness range, matrix stiffening promoted excessive F-actin polymerization and stress-fiber formation, producing a mechanically damped PM–actin interface that resisted membrane deformation and suppressed NP uptake. Pharmacological and genetic perturbations indicated that this mechanical barrier was reversible. In vivo, β-aminopropionitrile-mediated tumor softening loosened ECM architecture, increased NP penetration, and promoted cellular uptake by reducing F-actin-associated mechanical resistance. Intratumoral spatial analyses and paired bilateral tumor experiments further supported local regulation of NP uptake by the actomyosin state under matched matrix conditions. Combined tumor softening and donafenib-loaded PLGA NPs reduced endpoint tumor weight by 87.8% relative to free donafenib but increased pulmonary metastasis, revealing a potential efficacy-safety trade-off. These findings identify a multiscale mechanical mechanism linking tumor-matrix mechanics to nanomedicine delivery and…

items.title: Cycles upon cycles—Temperature scaling of medaka development
items.summary_raw: How organisms develop in dynamic environmental conditions is a fundamental question. We asked how day-night temperature cycles impact embryonic axis elongation and segmentation, itself a cyclic process linked to the segmentation clock, using the Japanese rice fish medaka. We developed an unbiased dimensional reduction approach, based on Singular Value Decomposition, to reliably identify the dynamic modes of segmentation clock oscillations across all temperature conditions. We reveal that the two major dynamic modes show opposite temperature sensitivities: While the temporal oscillation (mode 1) varies strongly with temperature, the spatial phase gradient (mode 2) appears largely temperature invariant. In addition, we found developmental parameters with intermediate, subscaled temperature responses, such as axis elongation. We used theoretical modeling to understand how dynamic modes emerge from the underlying local oscillation dynamics and axis elongation. We then exposed embryos to circadian and ultradian temperature cycles to reveal dynamic response patterns of oscillations and axis elongation, and found how these responses are integrated into morphological features. Combined, our theoretical–experimental results support a model in which the dynamic integration of temporal (i.e. segmentation clock related) and spatial (i.e. axis elongation) processes, in particular their subscaled temperature response patterns, quantitatively compensate each other to yield a robust…

items.title: Physics-informed single-frame end-to-end learning for denoising and background removal in fluorescence imaging
items.summary_raw: Fluorescence microscopy is often limited by low signal-to-noise ratios arising from the finite number of detected photons and by an out-of-focus background that obscures structural details. Here, we introduce a physics-informed end-to-end learning framework that enables denoising and background suppression from a single fluorescence image. By integrating a microscope-parameterized forward model, the proposed framework generates realistic training datasets entirely through simulation, eliminating the need for experimentally acquired ground-truth images. Once trained for a given imaging condition, the deep neural network can be deployed directly to previously unseen biological specimens without specimen-specific retraining, as demonstrated across the structurally distinct biological samples examined in this study. We experimentally validate the robust single-frame denoising performance in both wide-field and confocal fluorescence microscopy. The enhanced photon efficiency further enables superresolution optical fluctuation imaging using only tens of frames, substantially improving temporal resolution while preserving spatial fidelity. In addition, the proposed single-frame end-to-end learning framework can be extended to remove out-of-focus background in thick samples. These results establish physics-guided, simulation-based end-to-end learning as a general and practical strategy for rapid, data-efficient fluorescence image restoration under photon-limited conditions.

items.title: Spatiotemporal noise stabilizes unbounded diversity in strongly competitive communities
items.summary_raw: Classical ecological models predict that diverse communities should be unstable, presenting a central challenge to explaining the stable biodiversity seen in nature. We revisit this long-standing problem by extending the generalized Lotka–Volterra model to include both spatial structure and environmental fluctuations across space and time. We find that neither space nor environmental noise alone can resolve the tension between diversity and stability, but that together they permit arbitrarily many species to stably coexist in a sufficiently large system, despite strongly disordered competitive interactions. We analytically characterize the noise-induced transition to coexistence, showing that spatiotemporal noise drives power-law abundance fluctuations, leading to an anomalous scaling of moments known empirically as Taylor’s law. At the metacommunity level, this manifests as an emergent sublinear self-inhibition that stabilizes diversity and renders the interaction disorder irrelevant in the high-diversity limit. Spatiotemporal noise thus provides a resolution to the diversity-stability paradox and a generic mechanism by which complex communities can persist.

items.title: Latent causal diffusions for single-cell perturbation modeling
items.summary_raw: Perturbation screens hold the potential to systematically map regulatory processes at single-cell resolution, yet modeling and predicting transcriptome-wide responses to perturbations remains a major computational challenge. Existing methods often underperform simple baselines, fail to disentangle measurement noise from biological signal, and provide limited insight into the causal structure governing cellular responses. Here, we present the latent causal diffusion (LCD), a generative model that frames single-cell gene expression as a stationary diffusion process observed under measurement noise. LCD outperforms established approaches in predicting the distributional shifts of unseen perturbation combinations in single-cell RNA-sequencing screens while simultaneously learning a mechanistic dynamical system of gene regulation. To interpret these learned dynamics, we develop an approach we call causal linearization via perturbation responses (CLIPR), which yields an approximation of the direct causal effects between all genes modeled by the diffusion. CLIPR provably identifies causal effects under a linear drift assumption and recovers causal structure in both simulated systems and a genome-wide perturbation screen, where it clusters genes into coherent functional modules and resolves causal relationships that standard differential expression analysis cannot. The LCD-CLIPR framework bridges generative modeling with causal inference to predict unseen perturbation effects and…

items.title: Efficient and robust control with spikes that constrain free energy
items.summary_raw: Animal brains exhibit remarkable efficiency in perception and action, while being robust to both external and internal perturbations. The means by which brains accomplish this remains, for now, poorly understood, hindering our understanding of animal and human cognition, as well as our own implementation of efficient algorithms for control of dynamical systems. A potential candidate for a robust mechanism of state estimation and action computation is the free energy principle, but existing implementations of this principle have largely relied on conventional, biologically implausible approaches without spikes. We propose an efficient and robust spiking control framework with realistic biological characteristics. The resulting networks function as free energy constrainers, in which neurons only fire if they reduce the free energy of their internal representation. The networks offer efficient operation through highly sparse activity while matching performance with other similar spiking frameworks, and have high resilience against both external (e.g., sensory noise or collisions) and internal perturbations (e.g., synaptic noise and delays or neuron silencing) that such a network would be faced with when deployed by either an organism or an engineer. Overall, our work provides a mathematical account for spiking control through constraining free energy, providing both better insight into how brain networks might leverage their spiking substrate and a route for implementing…

items.title: Pyrrolysine supply and demand shapes the translational landscape in Methanosarcina acetivorans
items.summary_raw: The amber stop codon (UAG) can encode for pyrrolysine (Pyl) or be read as a stop codon by methylamine-metabolizing organisms including methanogenic archaea. The fate of UAG is decided during the decoding step of translation by competition between the pyrrolysine-aminoacylated transfer RNA (Pyl-tRNA Pyl ) and release factor. To further understand the consequences of pyrrolysine based genetic code expansion, we integrated RNA sequencing, tRNA charging analysis, and codon-resolved mono- and disome ribosome profiling in Methanosarcina acetivorans . During conditions of high pyrrolysine demand, we observed increased expression of the pyrrolysine biosynthetic operon with a concurrent increase in acylation of tRNA Pyl and ribosome occupancy at UAG codons. During low pyrrolysine demand, the population of Pyl-tRNA Pyl decreases and we observe a strong ribosome pausing signal during UAG decoding. We find that the dwell time on UAG codons is shorter during high demand, but ribosome collisions increase due to greater ribosome density on UAG-containing transcripts. Together, these results show how pyrrolysine demand modulates tRNA charging and controls elongation dynamics, clarifying the cellular consequences of decoding an ambiguous stop codon.

items.title: Mechanisms of intracellular pH gating and local anesthetic inhibition of the two-pore domain K + channel TASK-2
items.summary_raw: TWIK-related acid-sensitive K+ channel 2 (TASK-2) is a pH sensing two-pore K + (K2P) channel that regulates respiration in brainstem neurons and systemic pH homeostasis in kidney. Despite its physiological importance and implication in disease, the molecular basis for intracellular gating and pharmacological inhibition of TASK-2 is incompletely understood. Here, we combine cryo-EM and single-channel electrophysiology to resolve the mechanisms of TASK-2 gating by intracellular protons and inhibition by the anesthetic bupivacaine. We show protonation of intracellular lysines triggers a unique stacked gating mechanism distinct from other K + channels. Inner helices unwind and domain swap to form a β-zipper, which we call a Z-gate, that seals the cytoplasmic channel entrance. These conformational changes open lateral fenestrations to the membrane that permit lipids to invade the channel cavity and block the pore. Furthermore, we find bupivacaine inhibits the channel by competing with lipids in the cavity site in a state-dependent manner. These results define a paradigm for intracellular gating of K2Ps and provide a structural foundation for designing more potent and selective channel modulators.

items.title: Transcriptional regulation and function of GPR18 in macrophage subtype specification
items.summary_raw: Resolution of inflammation is mediated in part by agonists that engage immune cells to dampen inflammatory signaling, promote phagocytic functions, and facilitate tissue repair. G protein–coupled receptor 18 (GPR18) has emerged as an important proresolving receptor that is activated by endogenous mediators including Resolvin D2. However, very little is known about how GPR18 expression is controlled in immune cells, and its cell-autonomous roles during resolution of inflammation remain of interest. Here, we elucidated transcriptional and epigenetic regulation of Gpr18 in macrophages (MFs). We identified binding of monocyte/macrophage lineage-determining transcription factors (LDTFs) including PU.1, IRF8, and RUNX1 at the Gpr18 locus in the basal state in murine bone marrow–derived macrophages (BMDM). We found that Gpr18 is highly induced in BMDM by inflammatory stimuli including interferon gamma (IFNγ) and ligands for multiple toll-like receptors. Motif analysis predicted enrichment for LDTFs and signal-dependent TFs including nuclear factor κB (NFκB) and interferon regulatory factors (IRF) at the Gpr18 locus. Stimulation of BMDM with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or IFNγ increased the binding of NFκB p65 and IRF1 at the Gpr18 locus, which played a causal role in the induction of Gpr18 by LPS or IFNγ, respectively. items.title: Big Tech’s Nuclear Hedge
items.summary_raw: When America’s tech titans started plowing money into nuclear technology to power data centers in 2024, companies such as Google and Amazon opted to invest first in next-generation reactor startups. But electricity demand is soaring today, and those projects are still years away — at least — from generating power at reasonable commercial rates. So the industry is hedging by betting on existing nuclear plants to pump out more electricity in the near term. Uprates — renovations that allow nuclear operators to produce more power from existing reactors — are all the rage this year. In February, the Department of Energy issued its largest-ever loan to Southern Company to fund up to 6 gigawatts of uprates across the utility’s nuclear fleet. Last week, Amazon signed a deal with Constellation Energy, the nation’s largest operator of nuclear reactors, to uprate the Calvert Cliffs plant in Maryland to generate another 190 megawatts on top of its current 1.8-gigawatt output. Soon after, the Energy Department offered nuclear operator Vistra a $4 billion loan to uprate plants in Ohio and Pennsylvania. Then on Tuesday, Google inked its own deal with Constellation aimed at wringing out 890 megawatts of new power from 11 reactors across PJM Interconnection, the nation’s second-biggest and arguably most overworked grid system. “Everyone loves nuclear, but it takes a really long time to build,” Raiford Smith, Google’s head of power and energy for the cloud, told me yesterday. “The fastest way…

items.title: Low-Carbon Steel Company Hertha Metals Breaks Ground in Texas
items.summary_raw: The U.S. wants to make more of its own rare-earth magnets, which are critical to everything from guided missiles to aerospace systems and electric vehicle motors. But doing so will require a domestic source of high-purity iron, the main material in these magnets and one the U.S. imports almost entirely from China. Hertha Metals is betting it can fill that gap while helping decarbonize the ironmaking process, too. After raising a more than $133 million Series A, which the company announced last week, the Texas-based startup is promising to supply domestic magnet and steel manufacturers with 10,000 metric tons per year of lower-carbon, high-purity iron. That will come from its first commercial facility near Houston, where the company broke ground on Thursday. Steel customers, including automakers and other equipment manufacturers, have already expressed interest in Hertha’s tech. But the startup’s most important customer might be the federal government. Defense manufacturers depend on rare-earth magnets — which require 99.95% high-purity iron — for things like aerospace platforms and radar systems. That explains why the Department of Defense invested $65 million in Hertha’s Series A through its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program. The investment comes in partnership with the Economic Defense Unit, a new Pentagon division established under Trump that makes grants, loans, equity investments and purchase commitments into defense and dual-use sectors like critical…

items.title: Trump is gutting the Endangered Species Act. These 10 species show what’s at stake.
items.summary_raw: The Supreme Court once billed the Endangered Species Act as “the most comprehensive legislation for the preservation of endangered species ever enacted by any nation.” Federal protections have been key to saving nearly 300 U.S. species — including the bald eagle, American alligator, and grizzly bear — from permanent extinction. Each year, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, which is primarily responsible for implementing the law, evaluates species and lists them as “endangered” or “threatened.” When federal activity or private development has the potential to harm a listed species or its habitat, project developers are required to consult with the Service or obtain a permit prior to construction. For the last several decades, the interpretation of two words in particular — “take” and “harm” — have formed the backbone of the Nixon-era law. Its prohibition of “taking” an animal criminalized any attempts to “harass, harm, pursue, hunt, shoot, wound, kill, trap, capture, or collect” at-risk species. And the provision on “harm” ensured that degrading a listed species’ habitat could be penalized. These definitions have been key to the success of the law. But that all changed last month when the Trump administration determined that razing the habitat where endangered or threatened species breed, feed, and shelter would no longer face federal penalties. In a separate internal memo, the administration also reinterpreted the definition of “take,” limiting it to instances of…

items.title: From the farm to your door: How our global food system exploits workers
items.summary_raw: Like many big cities, New York teems with delivery workers who bring takeout, groceries, and any number of other things to anyone with a cellphone. They work at all hours and in all conditions, often without job security, health insurance, or even access to safe restrooms . They are often hit by cars, assaulted, or robbed. Many of them are Indigenous people from Guatemala and Mexico who left home to escape violence and the impacts of climate change. The worst impacts of that global crisis add to the risks those workers face . “When the city is hit with with massive snowstorms, floodings, or the recent smoke fires, many deliveristas are the ones who are on the front lines doing this work and responding to the climate crisis in order to take care of New Yorkers,” said Ligia Guallpa, who is Kichwa and the co-founder and executive director of the Worker’s Justice Project and Los Deliveristas Unidos. The organization organizes app-based delivery workers and advocates on their behalf. “But the reality is that often they cannot even take care of themselves.” A report released Monday says that exploitation is deeply embedded in the global food system, leaving many of the 1.4 billion people who produce, process, distribute, and deliver food poorly paid, inadequately protected , and vulnerable to abuse. items.title: An integrated framework for assessing future river basin sustainability using a CMIP6 multi-model ensemble in Australia
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate change is reshaping drought patterns across Australia, increasing pressure on water-resource security and highlighting the need for more informed and adaptive river-basin management. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of Australia’s future drought-related sustainability from 2031 to 2060 using a Quantile Delta Mapping-corrected, Taylor skill score-weighted multi-model ensemble, derived from ten CMIP6 global climate models (GCMs) under three emission scenarios (SSP245, SSP370, SSP585). The framework applies the standardized precipitation index (SPI) at 3- and 12-month timescales, bias-corrected using Quantile delta mapping, and integrates the reliability-resilience-vulnerability (RRV) methodology to evaluate drought persistence and systemic responses. The ensemble significantly reduced inter-model spread and precipitation biases relative to individual GCMs across diverse climate zones. Trend analysis revealed that decreasing and strongly decreasing annual precipitation trends together cover 57.2% of Australia under SSP245 and decreasing trends affect 59.2% under SSP370, whereas under SSP585 shows no clear trend, indicating greater uncertainty under extreme warming. Projections show intensification in drought duration and severity, particularly under SSP370 and SSP585, with the most spatially consistent increases concentrated across southwestern and southern Australia. items.title: Modeling optimal incentives for the electric vehicle market
Green acceleration, uneven sectoral change: Green industrial policy mixes and China's transition to electric mobility (2000−2022)
items.summary_raw: Green industrial policy has become increasingly important for understanding how the state shapes low-carbon industrial transitions, yet there remains limited explanation of how evolving policy configurations reshape sectoral systems over time, especially under latecomer conditions. Existing studies often focus on discrete outcomes such as innovation, diffusion or firm entry, rather than on how interacting policy instruments redirect the system of production and consumption. To address this gap, the study develops an analytical framework centred on green industrial policy, combining the policy mix lens with the sectoral system of innovation and production framework. The framework is applied to China's electric mobility transition between 2000 and 2022. Based on a longitudinal single-case study, the analysis combines qualitative content analysis and process tracing, drawing on 83 elite and expert interviews, six factory visits, and diverse secondary data. The study traces how China's green industrial policy mix cumulatively reconfigured the sectoral system through interacting supply-side, demand-side and coordination-oriented instruments. The analysis suggests that policy effects were mediated by sectoral structures, path-dependent dynamics and feedback loops. The “pure electric drive” strategy and complementary instrument mixes accelerated electric vehicle diffusion and supported the emergence of an indigenous power battery sector. However, this also generated uneven changes…

items.title: Revisit Intention Under Climate Risk in Island Tourism: Structural and Configurational Evidence from PLS-SEM and fsQCA
items.summary_raw: Climate risk increasingly shapes tourists’ judgements of safety, service continuity, and the viability of future trips to island destinations. Existing research has established the deterrent role of tourism risk, while giving less attention to how destination response capacity, climate information, and trust combine to preserve revisit intention. This study develops a threat-coping framework linking perceived climate risk (PCR), perceived destination climate resilience (PDCR), tourism climate-service usefulness (UTCS), destination trust (DT), and revisit intention (RI). An on-site survey of 480 Chinese tourists visiting Phuket was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). PLS-SEM showed a negative association between PCR and RI and positive associations for PDCR, UTCS, and DT. Trust had the strongest direct association with RI and partially transmitted the effects of both destination response resources. The structural model explained 74.6% of the variance in RI. fsQCA found no individually necessary condition and identified three sufficient configurations for each outcome. High RI arose from a resilience-trust route, a low-risk dual-resource route, and a low-risk climate-service-trust route. Low RI arose when low trust coincided with the joint absence of both response resources or when high risk combined with a deficit in either resource. Recalibration at the 10th, 50th, and 90th…

items.title: Eradicating or Managing Homelessness? A New Framework for Comparative Policy Framing
items.source_name: Journal of Comparative Policy Analysis Research and Practice
items.summary_raw: This article develops a six-dimensional framework for comparative policy framing and applies it to homelessness policy in England and Finland. Drawing on interviews with policymakers and practitioners, it shows that England’s approach is organised around a management-oriented frame centred on prevention, legal thresholds, and resource allocation, whereas Finland adopts an eradication-oriented frame grounded in universalism, housing as a right, and state responsibility. The findings demonstrate how interpretative frames structure policy ambition, institutional alignment, and implementation trajectories within contrasting welfare states.

items.title: Does solar interest extend to battery storage? Understanding shared and distinct motivators of adoption among German households
items.summary_raw: Household battery storage systems (BSSs) are increasingly installed alongside residential photovoltaics (PV), yet behavioral research on BSS adoption remains limited. This study investigates whether established frameworks explaining PV uptake extend to BSS adoption and whether households perceive the two technologies as distinct or interconnected. Using a proposed integrated framework combining insights from Diffusion of Innovations theory, Theory of Planned Behavior, and Value-Belief-Norm theory, we surveyed German households ( N = 371) and compared non-adopters, PV adopters, and PV-BSS adopters on psychological determinants of adoption. Despite PV being perceived as somewhat more visible, socially endorsed, and environmentally beneficial than BSSs, households did not appear to evaluate PV and BSS as entirely separate decisions. Compared to non-adopters, both adopter groups expressed more favorable beliefs about the technologies, with PV-BSS adopters perceiving the strongest benefits, lowest expense concerns, and reporting the highest personal innovativeness. Measurement model comparisons further indicated that PV- and BSS-specific beliefs were highly correlated, pointing to a unified decision-making structure. Structural equation modeling revealed that adoption intention was positively associated with personal norms to use renewable energy, perceived social approval, innovativeness, and perceived personal benefits, while expense concerns were related to lower intentions…

items.title: Harnessing Indigenous Knowledge for Climate-Smart Agri-Food Systems: A Review of Adaptation Strategies, Food Security, Ecosystem Services, Governance, and Digital Innovation in Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary_raw: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces escalating climate challenges that threaten agricultural productivity, food security, ecosystem sustainability, and rural livelihoods. Indigenous knowledge (IK), developed through generations of interaction with local environments, offers context-specific and culturally embedded solutions for climate adaptation and resilient agri-food systems. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on the role of indigenous knowledge in advancing climate-smart agriculture (CSA) and resilient agri-food systems across SSA. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), the review analyzed 17 studies published between 2000 and 2026. The findings reveal that indigenous knowledge contributes significantly to climate resilience through traditional weather forecasting, crop diversification, indigenous seed preservation, agroforestry, water harvesting, soil fertility management, and community-based natural resource governance. These practices enhance food security, livelihood resilience, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem service provision while strengthening adaptive capacity among smallholder farmers. The review further highlights the importance of inclusive governance frameworks, knowledge co-production, and policy support for integrating indigenous knowledge into climate adaptation and agricultural development strategies. Emerging digital technologies and innovation platforms also…

items.title: Modeling electricity price formation during Poland’s energy transition using market data and sentiment analysis
items.summary_raw: Electricity-price dynamics in energy-transitioning power systems reflect the interaction of fuel costs, carbon prices, financial conditions, regulatory information, and market expectations. This study examines whether text-derived news indicators provide incremental predictive information for Polish electricity prices. A curated English-language European policy-news corpus identified through a GDELT-assisted collection procedure is processed using two separate natural-language-processing branches. TF–IDF is used to characterize the thematic prominence of selected energy and climate-policy terms, while VADER is applied directly to article text to derive an interpretable news-tone indicator, referred to as the Climate Change News Index. These indicators are aligned with electricity, natural-gas, coal, oil, carbon-allowance, and equity-market variables. Ordinary Least Squares and Elastic Net models are evaluated using chronological out-of-sample forecasts. Market fundamentals remain the main predictive inputs, while the contribution of text-derived variables is small and specification-dependent. The results therefore indicate limited incremental predictive information rather than systematic forecasting superiority. The study is observational, and the reported relationships are interpreted as associative and predictive rather than causal. The proposed workflow provides a transparent way to incorporate policy-news information into electricity-price analysis. However, it does not…

items.title: How Words Build Worlds: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Trump’s 2025 UN Speech
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
items.summary_raw: This paper employs Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to examine a speech delivered by the U.S. President Donald Trump at the United Nations General Assembly in 2025. CDA investigates the nexus between language, power, and ideology, positing that discourse is not merely reflective but constitutive of social reality. This analysis deconstructs the linguistic strategies, including lexical choices, metaphorical framing, narrative structures, and stylistic deviations, to reveal how the speech constructs a Manichean worldview. This worldview posits a strong, resurgent America (“us”) against a backdrop of weak international institutions, hostile enemies, and misguided allies (“them”). The paper argues that the speech functions as a performative act of nationalist sovereignty, designed to delegitimize multilateralism, securitize immigration, and frame climate action as a destructive hoax, thereby advocating for a unilateralist approach to global governance.

items.title: Examining public acceptance of AI versus human-centric dementia care across NHS England’s dementia pathway stages
items.summary_raw: There are over five-hundred-thousand individuals with recorded dementia diagnoses in England, highlighting an urgent need for scalable and effective care solutions to ease pressure on health and social care systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled smart home systems are emerging as promising digital health innovations, offering cognitive support, real-time monitoring, and decision-making assistance. However, concerns around trust, user agency, and misconceptions about AI continue to limit acceptance and may hinder adoption. This study examined how stage of dementia care, system design, and level of system involvement shape public attitudes towards AI-driven care technologies. A repeated-measures design was employed, using vignettes that varied across three dimensions: stage of care (aligned with NHS England's Dementia Well Pathway), system centrism (AI-based versus human-based), and level of involvement (moderate support versus full control). Participants aged 55-64 years - a group at elevated risk of developing dementia or encountering these technologies within the next decade - rated each scenario on both acceptability and perceived likelihood of actualisation/plausibility. Findings showed that acceptability was sensitive to both care stage and system type. A significant interaction indicated that full human involvement was consistently rated as more acceptable, while AI involvement was viewed more favourably only at moderate levels. This interaction effect…

items.title: The politics of baselines: A political feasibility framework for energy and climate scenarios
items.summary_raw: Energy, transport, and climate scenarios rely on assumptions about future taxes, subsidies, and regulations, but such policy trajectories are rarely screened for political feasibility before they enter models. This paper addresses this often-neglected step in scenario design by developing a political feasibility framework to help modellers define and compare contested policy trajectories before quantification. Building on the distinction between outside and inside views of feasibility, the framework proceeds in two steps. First, it scopes a limited set of plausible trajectories using historical precedent, institutional practice, and actor commitments. Second, it evaluates them across five feasibility dimensions informed by institutional theory and political economy. The framework is demonstrated using a Swedish rail-demand forecast from 1999, in which a flat real road fuel tax path was used in the adopted-policy baseline. The case illustrates how seemingly neutral baseline assumptions embed political judgements and how a structured feasibility assessment can make alternative policy trajectories explicit and comparable. A simplified demand model is used to simulate the effect of alternative tax trajectories on rail demand. The framework offers scenario teams and modellers a practical approach to selecting and documenting policy assumptions based on political feasibility across adopted-policy, planned-policy, and exploratory scenario settings.

items.title: Climate Change Disinformation| Climate Change Disinformation—Introduction
items.summary_raw: In the Special Section “Climate Change Disinformation,” we examine climate-related disinformation at a transition point: It is increasingly less about denying climate science than it is about arguing against climate policy. Across six studies, the collection finds that denial of the science persists among those whose public case centers on cost and fairness. It also finds that disinformation succeeds where an audience is already disposed to accept it. In this introduction, we argue that this ongoing shift is outpacing the instruments built to address it, since arguments about policy are difficult to disprove and they largely remain beyond the reach of fact-checking or news literacy. The contributions offer researchers, practitioners, and policy makers a basis for responses that engage the politics of climate action rather than only factual claims of disinformation.

items.title: Climate risk and the production foundations of nutrition security: evidence from grain-supply capacity in Chinese cities
items.summary_raw: Introduction Climate risk poses growing challenges to food availability and the resilience of urban food systems. Methods Using panel data for 298 prefecture-level cities in China from 2010 to 2023, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the impact of climate risk on production-side food security, its transmission mechanisms, and regional heterogeneity. Results The results show that climate risk significantly reduces city-level grain output, and this finding remains robust to alternative specifications and endogeneity treatments. Mechanism analyses indicate that climate risk weakens food availability by adversely affecting agricultural mechanization, effective irrigation, grain-sown area, and fiscal support for agriculture. The negative effect is more pronounced in non-major grain-producing areas and regions with lower adaptive capacity. Further analysis suggests that climate risk also undermines agricultural economic performance and food-supply stability. Discussion These findings provide city-level evidence on how climate shocks affect production-side food security and highlight the importance of strengthening agricultural production conditions and adaptive capacity to enhance food-system resilience and safeguard nutrition security.

items.title: The cost of regulatory delay: quantifying how permitting timelines affect offshore wind energy costs
items.summary_raw: Abstract Rapid deployment of offshore renewable energy and transmission infrastructure can be a major contributor to energy system decarbonization. However, regulatory obligations frequently impose deployment delays that are typically not quantified in cost terms. The costs of such delays should be incorporated in project and technology assessments. Here, a framework is developed that treats the development lag between project inception and operation as a temporal proxy for regulatory and related obligations, and propagates it through a levelized-cost-of-energy calculation to quantify the cost of delay. This framework is used to compare, on a common basis, conventional high-voltage cable transmission with offshore power-to-hydrogen (PtH) alternatives. The framework is applied to three strategies to move energy to shore from offshore wind facilities. The results show that for an example, one gigawatt plant, deploying one year sooner can save €110 million—a relevant metric to gauge the cost of policy designed to expedite deployment. In scenarios where the PtH can be deployed faster than high-voltage cables, the results suggest a limited decision space in which PtH transmission is cheaper, indicating that it will need to realize other benefits to compete with high-voltage cable transmission on cost. Profitability between electricity-based and hydrogen-based transmission is then compared, considering differences in deployment time. There are existing conditions of hydrogen and…

items.title: Influence of Political Climate on Literary Production in Nigeria
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
items.summary_raw: This study examines the influence of political climate on literary production in Nigeria, focusing on how political events, governance structures, and socio-political tensions shape literary creativity and thematic choices. The main objective is to analyze the relationship between Nigeria’s political environment and the production, dissemination, and reception of literary works. Using a desk research methodology, the study reviews scholarly works, policy reports, and literary analyses from colonial to contemporary periods. Findings reveal that political regimes, censorship, and socio-political unrest significantly affect the themes, genres, and publication of literary works. Writers often respond to political crises through satire, allegory, and protest literature, reflecting society’s anxieties and aspirations. The study concludes that the political climate acts both as a catalyst and constraint for literary expression. It contributes to understanding the intersection of politics, culture, and literature in Nigeria.

items.title: Research on the Intelligent Transformation Path of the Port and Logistics Electromechanical Industry
items.summary_raw: The port and logistics electromechanical industry underpins port production and supply chain operation, and its level of intelligentization is directly related to the improvement of operational efficiency and industrial capacity. This paper reviews the evolution of this industry from equipment-dominated and system integration toward intelligentization, and, in combination with the implementation of three types of technologies—the Internet of Things and 5G communication, artificial intelligence and big data, and intelligent control and digital twin—in terminals, discusses the drivers behind the shift of the industry's center of value toward software and algorithmic capabilities. Among these, the position of the software segment, represented by the Terminal Operating System (TOS) and the Equipment Control System (ECS), in the industrial chain keeps rising, and the traditional division of labor formed around equipment manufacturing is being adjusted accordingly. On this basis, the paper puts forward suggestions on the transformation path from three dimensions—layered advancement, industrial coordination, and policy support—for reference by the port electromechanical industry.

items.title: From participation to decision-making in energy infrastructure siting: A framework for operationalizing public influence with a case study of nuclear waste in Canada
items.summary_raw: The global deployment of new energy infrastructure is influenced by how institutions manage engagements with the public and potentially impacted communities. While existing scholarship often focuses on the extent of public participation, it can fail to account for how public input is translated into binding decision outcomes. This gap can lead to procedural “box-checking” and, ultimately, public backlash. We argue that this shortcoming stems from conflating public participation (the process of engagement) with public influence (the conditions and pathways for public input to shape decisions). This study introduces the Public Influence Pathways (PIP) Framework, which operationalizes public influence as a bridge that links public participation with institutional decision-making across four elements: entry points, influence approaches, mechanisms, and decision uptake. The case of Canada's siting process for a used nuclear fuel repository is employed to demonstrate the framework's diagnostic utility. Our findings show that limiting formal entry points can drive unresolved claims to alternate channels for public influence, and that connecting decision stages with participation can allow for learning and adaptation. Ultimately, the framework provides planners and scholars with traceability of public influence, as well as a means to account for structural flexibility, foster co-production, and assess socio-technical readiness for critical infrastructure siting.

items.title: Environmental Attitudes Among Undergraduate Students: Implications for Environmental Literacy
items.summary_raw: Understanding environmental attitudes (EA) is important in higher education because universities play a significant role in shaping students’ environmental awareness and dispositions. Environmental attitudes are an important component of environmental literacy, which encompasses the knowledge, skills, and dispositions needed to understand and address environmental issues. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the environmental attitudes of undergraduate students from two universities in Labuhanbatu Regency, Indonesia (n = 312), and to analyze their association with selected demographic characteristics. A structured questionnaire was used to collect demographic information, while environmental attitudes were assessed using the 24-item Environmental Attitudes Inventory (EAI-24). The EAI-24 assesses 12 dimensions of environmental attitudes representing preservation- and utilization-oriented perspectives. The results showed that students’ environmental attitudes tended to favor utilization-oriented perspectives over conservation-oriented perspectives. Significant differences in environmental attitudes were also found across demographic characteristics, particularly gender and ethnicity. These findings indicate a weakness in the affective dimension of environmental literacy and highlight the need for context-sensitive environmental education that considers students’ demographic and cultural backgrounds. The findings have practical implications for developing targeted…

items.title: Weeds as teachers on country: Management through seasonal story calendars
items.summary_raw: This paper reconceptualises weeds through Australian Indigenous knowledge systems, presenting them not as invasive threats, but as teachers; living beings that offer ecological insight, support restoration, and contribute to cultural renewal and resurgence. Drawing on relational governance theories, the study employs Indigenous methodologies, including yarning with Country and the development of a storying seasonal calendar, to examine the behaviours and teachings of Fireweed (Senecio madagascariensis), African Lovegrass (Eragrostis curvula ), and Lantana (Lantana camara). Through attentive engagement with these plants across the seasons, the research reveals how each species responds to ecological disturbance in ways that reflect deeper patterns of damage, resilience, and adaptation. Fireweed emerges as a guard of soil exhaustion and overgrazing, while African Lovegrass plays a stabilising role in degraded landscapes during ecological transitions, and Lantana offers both refuge and warning through a chemically mediated defence of disturbed ground. These findings unsettle adversarial and militaristic paradigms of weed management and instead highlight the importance of Country-centred, seasonal, and relational approaches. By weaving Indigenous knowledge with ecological observation, the paper demonstrates that weeds are not only invasive but also teachers, whose messages can guide more ethical and restorative forms of environmental governance. • Weeds can be ecological…

items.title: Integrated Farming Cafeteria: A General Frame-Work for Promoting Integrated Farming at Land-Scape Level
items.summary_raw: Integrated farming, encompassing precisely a synergistic combination of crops, agroforestry and livestock, is needed to attain sustainability and economic viability of farms and address challenges of climate change. The approach offers a holistic solution to the challenges of monoculture systems dependent upon a few selected crops. Integrated farming must be flexible enough to accommodate new innovations in crops, cultivars or other changes to optimize resource use and to meet demands. This essentially requires exposure of farming community to combinations of innovations and alternative options. To fulfil this objective, we describe here the concept of Integrated Farming Cafeteria (IFC), its uniqueness and relevance to promote integrated farming at land-scape level. IFC established at the ICAR-Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur on 2.1 ha in 2022, accommodated 130 varieties of 16 field crops, 9 of five horticultural crops and 10 of eight fodder crops, grown with recommended practices, in addition to several soil and water conservation technologies (residue recycling, water harvesting, micro-irrigation) and other interventions (solar pump, precision farming, boundary plantation) that reduce cost of production and enhance income from farming. More than 5800 farmers visited IFC, from 2022 to 2025 with a well-defined purpose to personally witness and compare the advantages of water and soil management practices, new crops and improved crop varieties over their…

items.title: Salt Cavern Hydrogen Storage for Renewable‐Dominated Smart Energy Systems
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy increasingly face balancing challenges that extend beyond intraday variability to multiday shortages, seasonal mismatch, resource adequacy and system resilience. Salt cavern hydrogen storage (SCHS) has emerged as a promising underground hydrogen storage option for renewable‐dominated smart energy systems. It can act as the large‐scale storage component that connects renewable hydrogen production with downstream hydrogen use and power‐to‐hydrogen‐to‐power pathways. This review examines SCHS from a power‐system integration perspective. It synthesises the geological and operational characteristics that enable large‐scale hydrogen storage. It then evaluates the contributions of SCHS to renewable integration, multi‐timescale flexibility, clean firm capacity, ancillary services and resilience. The review also examines modelling approaches for coupled electricity–hydrogen systems, including cavern constraints, intertemporal dynamics and cross‐sector coordination. It further discusses the policy, regulatory and market conditions required for large‐scale deployment. SCHS is not a universal storage technology. It is a context‐dependent infrastructure option whose value becomes most important in renewable‐dominated power systems where short‐duration storage alone cannot meet long‐duration flexibility and reliability needs.

items.title: Climate Change scholarship on Lahore: A thematic review
items.source_name: Journal of Emerging Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities
items.summary_raw: Climate change has become a major challenge for rapidly growing cities, particularly in the Global South. Lahore, Pakistan’s second-largest city, faces increasing climate-related risks, including rising temperatures, smog, the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, air pollution, groundwater depletion, and urban flooding. This review examines the existing literature on climate change in Lahore by analysing key research themes, methodological approaches, and policy discussions. Using a thematic review approach, the study synthesises evidence from published academic studies and relevant policy documents. The findings show that rapid urbanization, land use change, weak environmental governance, and ineffective policy implementation have increased the city’s climate vulnerability. Recent research has improved understanding through geospatial technologies and interdisciplinary studies. However, intersectional studies on climate change in Lahore that seek to explore variables such as class, gender, age, and disability are needed to fulfil the important gaps that remain in climate governance and adaptation. This review also identifies these gaps and highlights the need for stronger institutions, evidence-based planning, and inclusive climate policies to improve urban climate resilience in Lahore.

items.title: Climate Change Disinformation| Harvesting Denial: Mapping Primary and Secondary Climate Obstruction in Brazil
items.summary_raw: This study conducts a qualitative, exploratory investigation of climate obstruction in Brazil. Based on a literature review and an exploratory analysis of gray literature, the study maps the key players, narratives, tactics, and institutional linkages that shape climate obstruction in Brazil. By examining how obstruction spreads across political, economic, and media spheres, the study identifies patterns that mirror and diverge from those in the Global North, particularly the United States, where obstruction has longer-established roots. The analysis also discusses the recent evolution of the phenomenon into new forms of climate obstruction. Findings show that Brazilian obstruction operates as an orchestrated ecosystem primarily sponsored by agribusiness, with practical consequences for public policy. This ecosystem gained greater prominence and institutional legitimacy during the Bolsonaro administration (2019–2022), establishing obstruction as a political force rather than a discursive norm.

items.title: Framing nature‐based solutions in Norwegian public media: A critical discourse analysis of public narratives
items.summary_raw: Abstract Nature‐based solutions (NbS) have become central to environmental governance. Yet, their societal legitimacy depends on how they are framed in public discourse. This study investigates how Norwegian media actors construct narratives around NbS, whose voices are amplified, and the extent to which plural and Indigenous epistemologies are represented. We conducted a critical discourse analysis of 57 articles published between 2018 and 2025 across five major Norwegian media outlets. Articles were coded abductively, drawing on typologies of values (instrumental, relational and intrinsic) and dimensions of environmental justice. The sample primarily included opinion pieces and expert contributions, most of which were authored by non‐journalist experts. Four dominant narratives emerged: (1) Nature as infrastructure , emphasising technical and cost‐effective climate services; (2) Win‐win optimism , framing NbS as universally beneficial; (3) Nature as relationship , depicting nature as a partner but remaining marginal; and (4) Commodification critiques , primarily in progressive outlets. In addition, we identified a patterned absence of Indigenous epistemologies , with Sámi perspectives almost entirely absent. Outlet‐specific patterns reflected editorial ideologies, with instrumental framings dominating across the corpus. Our findings highlight that Norwegian media discourses on NbS remain strongly anthropocentric, which may contribute to reinforcing perceptions of nature as…

items.title: Hydrogen’s future in Türkiye: Storage, natural gas integration, and energy transition
items.source_name: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
items.summary_raw: Hydrogen stands out as a clean energy carrier that plays a critical role in the global energy transformation. Türkiye's increasing energy demand, dependence on fossil fuels, and carbon emission reduction targets place hydrogen technologies at the center of national energy policies. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the integration of hydrogen into energy systems could contribute to reducing global carbon emissions by up to 20%. This study comprehensively examines Türkiye's hydrogen potential, its integration with existing energy infrastructure, and hydrogen storage solutions. The study provides a detailed analysis of compressed gas, liquid hydrogen, solid-state storage, and underground storage technologies. Türkiye's existing geological structure was determined to be suitable for underground hydrogen storage, but infrastructure deficiencies were highlighted as a significant obstacle. Furthermore, factors such as technical challenges encountered in integrating hydrogen into natural gas networks, pipeline material compatibility, and the risk of hydrogen embrittlement were discussed. In addition, the potential for hydrogen's use in various sectors, such as industry, transportation, and energy production, has been explored. For example, the use of hydrogen in iron and steel production can reduce carbon emissions by up to 90% compared to traditional methods. It has been demonstrated that hydrogen fuel cell vehicles can provide an alternative to fossil fuel…

items.title: The moralization paradox at work: How Supervisor's moral framing depletes subordinates' self‐regulatory resources and suppresses proactive problem prevention
items.source_name: Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology
items.summary_raw: Abstract Integrating moral and ethical considerations into work is often presumed to yield a wide range of beneficial outcomes. Yet these benefits may not be unconditional, as prevailing scholarship has largely overlooked the potential costs associated with self‐regulatory resource depletion and diminished self‐initiated behaviours that are critical for averting future work disruptions. Drawing on ego depletion theory, we theorize that supervisor's work moralization can inadvertently hinder subordinates' proactive problem prevention by elevating their experiences of ego depletion. Furthermore, we posit that subordinates' reflective moral attentiveness intensifies this relationship, such that highly reflective individuals are more susceptible to the depleting effects of supervisor's work moralization, which in turn exacerbates the reduction in their proactive problem prevention. To test these propositions, we conducted two complementary empirical studies: Study 1, an experience sampling investigation, and Study 2, a vignette‐based laboratory experiment. Across both studies, the findings robustly supported our hypotheses. This research advances the literature by challenging the predominantly positive narrative of work moralization, illuminating its paradoxical potential to undermine subordinates' proactive behaviours, and providing novel theoretical insight into the boundary conditions and self‐regulatory mechanisms shaping the consequences of moral framing in the workplace.

items.title: Communication Strategies and Effects of Public Policy Advocacy on Social Media Platforms: A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Framing, Engagement, and Policy Influence
items.summary_raw: In this paper we examine the use of framing by advocacy organizations and government entities in social media to advance public policy goals and the effect of those strategies on different types of citizen response. We adopt a sequential explanatory mixed methods design by combining quantitative content analysis of a 2340-policy related posts from Twitter/X, Facebook, and Instagram with semi-structured interviews of 24 communication professionals. The sample comprised 20 public-facing organizations operating in one national context, in four policy domains – healthcare, environmental policy, education and social welfare. Five framing categories – diagnostic, prognostic, motivational, episodic, and thematic – were operationalised and evaluated against publicly available engagement metrics (likes/reactions, shares/reposts and comments), while click-through rate was evaluated separately where organisation-level analytics were accessible. Motivational framing generated more total engagement, but episodic framing generated more substantive comment-based participation. Differences across platforms demonstrate that predominantly visually-oriented environments support motivational and narrative frames, and platforms with more supports for text and links support solution-oriented and deliberative policy talk. According to interview results, we can explain this pattern by an engagement – depth paradox: Practitioners need attention maximizing content and at the same time want to be able…

items.title: Double energy vulnerability in Eastern Europe: quantifying and verifying regional sensitivity to the phenomenon
items.summary_raw: This study considers 57 regions from 8 Eastern European countries and quantifies the sensitivity to double energy vulnerability of each region by developing a composite indicator. Double energy vulnerability is a concept describing simultaneous exposure to energy and transport poverty. Eastern European countries present high levels of double energy vulnerability; nonetheless, remaining an understudied macro-region. To understand the dependency between double energy vulnerability and rurality and tenure, the results are then compared with the rurality levels of the different regions, and to the national proportion spent on energy and transport services. The developed indicator provides an analysis of the phenomenon across Eastern Europe, quantifying regions' sensitivity to it by combining indicators stemming from different dimensions. Data from 2015 to 2024 was considered. Bulgaria is found to be the country presenting the highest level of double energy vulnerability. For the latter specifically, data at higher spatial resolution was utilised to have a more detailed understanding and to assess the obtained results. Finally, the results were verified by performing interviews with relevant experts in the field, considering also non-quantifiable aspects. The results provide a clearer picture of Eastern European regions' sensitivity to double energy vulnerability, highlighting the most sensitive ones.

items.title: Climate policy uncertainty and agricultural digital-intelligent transformation in China: evidence from provincial panel data
items.summary_raw: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. Methods Using panel data from 31 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2022, we construct an agricultural digital-intelligent transformation index. A two-way fixed effects model, instrumental variable estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and moderation tests are adopted for empirical analysis. Results The results show that climate policy uncertainty significantly inhibits agricultural digital-intelligent transformation, and this negative effect remains evident after addressing potential endogeneity. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the inhibitory effect is significant only in regions with moderately developed digital finance and in major grain-consuming areas. Further analysis shows that loans to agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry and fishery industries and the pilot policy for full-process socialized agricultural services positively moderate this relationship and weaken the adverse effect of climate policy uncertainty. Discussion These findings contribute to the literature on climate policy uncertainty and sustainable agricultural transformation by linking policy…

items.title: Climate Change Disinformation| Climate Denialism as a Discursive Dynamic: Truth (and Politics) Beyond Facts
items.summary_raw: Applying Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) methods to the online output of climate change contesters, this article examines how their discursive strategies are accommodated within counter-disinformation frameworks. Critiquing the reductive epistemology shaping such frameworks, it challenges the notion that, by endorsing “depoliticized understandings” based on unassailable scientific authority, they build democratic consensus from a factually validated decarbonization imperative. It argues that unless facts generated within the scientific paradigm are incorporated into an agonistic process within which their articulation with truth remains contingent, they cannot effectively combat climate contestation.

items.title: Examination of Climate Change Attitude Among Junior High School Students: A Gender Gap Analysis and Scale Evaluation using Rasch Model
items.source_name: Jurnal Pembelajaran Bimbingan dan Pengelolaan Pendidikan
items.summary_raw: Climate change has become one of the most critical environmental issues affecting human life and environmental sustainability. Students’ climate change attitudes play an important role in developing environmental awareness and responsible behavior from an early age. However, studies investigating students’ climate change attitudes using the Rasch model are still limited, particularly among junior high school students in Indonesia. Therefore, this study aimed to analyze junior high school students’ climate change attitudes using Rasch analysis and to identify gender-based differences in students’ responses. This study employed a descriptive quantitative design involving 25 ninth-grade students consisting of 11 male and 14 female students from a junior high school in Blora Regency, Central Java, Indonesia. The instrument used was the Climate Change Attitude Survey (CCAS) consisting of 33 Likert-scale items. The data were examined using the Rasch model utilizing Winsteps 4.4.5 software. The findings revealed that students’ climate change attitudes were still at a moderate level. In the beliefs indicator, only 20% of students were categorized as good, while in the intentions indicator, 36% were categorized as good. The Rasch analysis showed that person reliability was 0.90 and item reliability was 0.88, representing that the instrument had good consistency and reliability. Differential Item Functioning (DIF) analysis showed that most items did not exhibit gender bias, except…

items.title: Perceptions of Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Climate Resilience, among Urban Residents Living with Asthma: An Exploratory Qualitative Study
items.summary_raw: Abstract In the US, rates of asthma, and in particular, uncontrolled asthma, are disproportionately high among historically marginalized racial/ethnic groups and among urban residents. Against the backdrop of climate change and its known consequences, which can exacerbate the environmental triggers of asthma, these inequities are further magnified. This qualitative study explored perceptions of climate change, health impacts, and climate resilience among historically marginalized urban adults with asthma. Black/African-American, Hispanic/Latino, and/or multiracial adults ( $$\ge$$ ≥ 18 years) diagnosed with asthma, and residing in the Chicagoland area, were recruited. Semistructured interviews informed by the capability, opportunity, motivation, and behavior (COM-B) model were conducted, and data were transcribed for thematic coding. Data from 20 interviews revealed four primary themes: (1) climate change awareness, (2) perceived harms of climate change, (3) climate resiliency: barriers and strategies, and (4) perceived outlook on climate change. Participants consistently associated extreme weather with adverse asthma management consequences and highlighted the negative impacts of climate-related events on their outdoor time, physical activity, and social life. Virtually all participants emphasized significant financial burden resulting from their daily living adaptations for managing their condition in the context of climate change. Participants showed variable levels of…

items.title: Habitat Suitability Modeling of Bombus affinis under Climate Change
items.summary_raw: The North American bumble bee Bombus affinis (B. affinis) is an important wild pollinator that has experienced severe population declines since the late 20th century. However, spatially explicit assessments of how climate change and human activities jointly shape its distribution remain limited, constraining forward-looking conservation planning. Here, we used a maximum entropy model (MaxEnt), integrating species occurrence records with multidimensional environmental variables, to characterize the historical distribution of B. affinis and project changes in potential habitat suitability under different climate scenarios for the mid- and late 21st century. The results show that mean temperature of the warmest quarter was the dominant predictor of its distribution, contributing 59.0% to the model. Moreover, our model indicated a highly restricted historical distribution, with medium- and high-suitability habitats (suitability > 0.7) accounting for only 7.9% of the study area and concentrated along the North Atlantic coast, the Great Lakes region, and the Appalachian Mountains. By the late 21st century, the SSP585 high-emission pathway would cut both the size and the quality of suitable habitats markedly; the range would also contract northward, shifting away from the south-central and northeastern United States toward higher latitudes and finally into southern Canada. This work gives a quantitative evaluation of B. affinis habitat suitability in both historical and future…

items.title: The Politics of the “Non-Political”: A Conceptual Review
items.summary_raw: Recent literature has documented a growing entanglement between political processes and many nonpolitical entities. This calls into question the traditional presupposition of politics as a self-contained sphere, highlighting the need to clarify how the conceptual relationship between the political and the nonpolitical has been established. In line with a relational understanding of politics, we provide a boundary analysis by looking at the “non-political” labeling in 140 empirical studies published in political science and communication journals. Two major conceptual treatments are identified: categorical, treating the “non-political” as an inherent, exclusive feature; and contextual, viewing it as a temporary, transformative state. Intellectual traditions, theoretical orientations, methodological standards, and rhetorical norms in academic knowledge production may explain why this boundary has been constructed in such different ways. We call for a more active reconciliation between these treatments, and argue that the nonpolitical, as well as (de)politicization, should be recognized as a meaningful analytical lens. It signifies a relational stance against the explicit, institutionalized politics in political communication studies, offering an indirect yet heuristically productive response to the question of what the political is.

items.title: Dunaj u Bratislavy má nejméně vody v historii
items.summary_raw: Dunaj na vodoměrném profilu Devín na okraji Bratislavy dosáhl historického minima. Od začátku měření v roce 1900 nebyl jeho denní průtok nikdy nižší. Dosavadní rekord vydržel 117 let. Slovensko trápí mimořádné sucho už řadu měsíců, v dalších dnech by se ale situace měla alespoň přechodně zlepšit. Více na novinky.cz zde .

items.title: Climate Change Disinformation| Seeking the Truth Among Dead Crops: Carbon Footprint Victimhood, Platformed Conspiracism, and Climate Countermovement in Turkey
items.summary_raw: After years of climate inaction, Turkey’s ratification of the Paris Agreement in 2021 prompted the Justice and Development Party’s discursive shift from high-carbon hegemonic agenda to green developmentalist rhetoric. This policy change provoked a backlash among conspiratorial climate-denial networks on social media. When the country’s worst-ever wildfires in 2021 were followed by wheat field fires in 2022, far-right and nationalist coalitions on X disseminated the conspiracy theory that foreign actors deliberately set these fires to undermine Turkey’s food sovereignty and engineer demographic decline under the cover of the climate agenda. Drawing on critical discourse analysis, we examine tweets from 2 major hashtag campaigns linking these fires to climate conspiracy theories. Our analysis identifies 3 interconnected motivational themes: environmental nationalism, economic injustice, and population control, each framed through a rhetoric of moral decay that sustains nationalist resentment and a discourse of victimhood.

items.title: Why we need a bespoke approach to managing energy in short-term lettings: a relational case study of domestic decarbonisation in England
items.summary_raw: Extended abstract 7-092-26 Short-term lettings (STLs) have grown rapidly in England, concentrated in cities, national parks, and coastal towns. While policy debates focus on housing affordability and social impacts, the link between STLs and building energy efficiency remains unexplored. Simultaneously, domestic decarbonisation is critical for meeting UK climate targets. This research uses Whitstable, Kent, a coastal town with high STL density, to examine whether bespoke, place-based strategies are needed to manage domestic energy demand. It explores how STLs influence local decarbonisation compared to other housing tenures, what social, spatial, and regulatory factors shape energy management in STL-dense areas, and whether tourism dynamics create hidden barriers to retrofit and how policy might address them. The design is qualitative, combining interviews, participant observation, online forum analysis, and QGIS-based spatial mapping. This mixed-method approach examines structural conditions and lived experiences, revealing how STLs are embedded in Whitstable’s social and regulatory environment. Fieldwork begins in April. This presentation will share initial findings from spatial mapping and forum analysis. Early patterns show STLs clustering in popular areas link to harder-to-decarbonise buildings. Forum data reveals strong social tensions, raising questions around retrofit decision making, and Intermediaries, management companies, and absentee owners may affect engagement…

items.title: Compound climatic extreme events amplify food insecurity
items.summary_raw: The increasing co-occurrence of climatic hazards poses growing risks to crop production, yet their implications for rice supply and self-sufficiency remain insufficiently quantified. Here, we combine a vine-copula framework with calibrated ORYZA (v3) model to characterize nonlinear dependencies among climate indicators, estimate the probability of compound climatic events, and assess their impacts on rice yield potential, yield gaps, and national self-sufficiency across major rice-growing regions of China. We show that (1) intensification of the global water cycle increases the frequency of extreme heat from 25 to 50% in the late 20th century to over 90% by 2050, while the risk of compound events involving extreme heat, rainfall and/or solar radiation is projected to change by approximately 3–50% in single-rice systems and 1–60% in double-rice systems relative to 1981–2017; (2) increasing probability of compound climatic extreme events apparently affect potential production for single rice (−2.8 to 0.2 t ha −1 ) and double-rice growing systems (−1.3 to 0.8 t ha −1 ), with downside risk increasing progressively over time; (3) the negative impacts on rice yield potential outweigh the benefits (0.5 to 1.5 t ha −1 ) gained from increased atmospheric CO 2 , leading to reduction in yield gaps. Assuming production remains near 70% of yield potential, projected national rice supply in 2030–2050 (∼216 Mt. with CO 2 effects; ∼195 Mt. without) may fall below projected demand (∼220 Mt)…

items.title: How does climate risk affect fisheries? New evidence from the operating cash flows of Chinese listed firms
items.summary_raw: Listed fisheries companies depend heavily on natural conditions, leaving their operations particularly exposed to climate change. Using Chinese listed fisheries companies as the research sample, this study examines the effect of regional climate risk on operating cash flow and investigates potential mitigating mechanisms. The results show that regional climate risk significantly reduces operating cash flow. Further analysis indicates that extreme heat, cold, rainfall, and drought all weaken corporate cash flow, demonstrating the multidimensional nature of climate exposure in fisheries. Government subsidies and stronger internal governance mitigate these adverse effects and therefore serve as important buffers against climate shocks. By documenting the cash-flow consequences of climate risk, this study provides new firm-level evidence on how environmental shocks affect fisheries operations and offers practical implications for strengthening climate resilience in the sector.

items.title: Policy–Industry–Import Security Coordination in Japan’s Hydrogen Energy System Under Geopolitical Risk
items.summary_raw: Japan’s hydrogen strategy faces three interrelated challenges in policy support, industrial deployment, and import security. This study builds a three-system framework covering policy, industry, and import security, and evaluates their coupling coordination in Japan from 2017 to 2025 using an entropy-weighted method and a coupling coordination degree model. A geopolitical impulse weighting factor based on Japan’s annual geopolitical risk index is further introduced to examine how external shocks reshape coordination. Results show moderate-to-high coupling but persistently low coordination. The policy and industry subsystems show partial co-movement in the earlier period but diverge more clearly after 2022, while the unweighted import-security subsystem also weakens after peaking around 2022. Geopolitical-risk adjustment further lowers coordination after 2022 without changing the overall temporal pattern. From a sustainability perspective, these findings suggest that Japan’s hydrogen transition requires better coordination among policy support, industrial development, and resilient supply structures. The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for assessing the coordination and sustainability of hydrogen transitions in energy-constrained economies.

items.title: Climate Change Disinformation| Unraveling Debunked Climate Change Disinformation and Responses to Fact-Checks: Evidence From the United States, Netherlands, and Philippines
items.summary_raw: Although climate change skepticism and denialism have been considered influential narratives in the contemporary digital information landscape, we know little about how such narratives are legitimized in climate change disinformation across different national settings. Against this background, this study relies on an in-depth qualitative content analysis of fact-checked disinformation in the Netherlands, the United States, and the Philippines as contrasting global cases. In addition, to explore the level of resistance to fact-checks, social media comments in response to fact-checking information were analyzed inductively. Our main findings indicate that climate skepticism was often constructed by deceptively re-interpreting, de-contextualizing, delegitimizing, or altering expert knowledge and scientific evidence. Disinformation claims and responses often used a populist logic, for which common sense and direct observations were juxtaposed to the alleged dishonesty of scientists. Responses to fact-checks mostly reinforced disinformation or challenged the fact-checker, which offers limited support for the real-life effectiveness of climate change debunks.
