items.title: The Crucial Hardhat Union That Has Yet to Endorse the Permitting Bill
items.summary_raw: Building trades want to build. This desire for more and better big projects has meant that unions representing construction workers, utility linemen, operating engineers, plumbers, pipefitters, and so on have spent past decade-plus ping-ponging between praise and exasperation toward major Democratic priorities, especially when it comes to climate and energy policy. Now, with a permitting bill negotiated by two Democrats and two Republicans in the Senate, much of the hardhat union sector is signing on as eager supporters. If the rest of the Democratic coalition can sign on to the bill, it may go some way to repairing a breach that has been widening since the Obama administration. The modern fight over U.S. energy infrastructure began with a Canadian pipeline project. Building trades were some of the most fervent advocates for the Keystone XL pipeline , which would have brought oil from the tar sands of Canada’s Alberta province into the continental United States — a project that Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden both opposed and which the latter finally canceled in 2021. In the interim, the first Trump administration tested these unions’ historic allegiance with Democrats as the left became more vocal on climate policy. items.title: AZEC 2.0に向けて：フィリピンの動向
items.summary_raw: 日本が主導する脱炭素の地域連携枠組みであるアジア・ゼロエミッション共同体（AZEC）。2026年に入り、AZECを取り巻く状況は大きく変化しています。日本が燃料の安定供給に重点を置く一方、多くのパートナー国はクリーンエネルギーの導入をさらに加速させたいと考えています。その一つが、今年のAZEC首脳会合・閣僚会合の開催国であるフィリピンです。フィリピンを対象とした最新のケーススタディは、電力系統の整備やクリーンエネルギーの導入拡大において、AZECを通じた協力の余地が大きいことを示しています。 東南アジア諸国は、事実上のホルムズ海峡封鎖と、その結果生じたエネルギー市場危機で深刻な影響を受けています。日本はこの危機を受け、AZECイニシアチブの更新を発表し、エネルギー強靭化を中核に据えた「AZEC 2.0」、及びパートナー国のエネルギー調達を支援する金融面での協力パッケージとして、100億ドル規模の「アジア・エネルギー・資源供給力強靱化パートナーシップ」、通称「POWERR Asia（パワー・アジア）」構想を立ち上げました。目下の危機への対応に追われる国々への資金支援は歓迎すべきですが、その一方で、今回の発表を受け、同構想が短期・長期の双方で化石燃料を軸とした方策に偏りかねないという懸念も生じています。 こうした変化の中でも、日本とパートナー国間の具体的なプロジェクトや投資の促進が、引き続きAZECの中核的な役割を担うことに変わりはありません。AZECの案件につき2025年に当団体が発表した最初の分析では、こうした案件の内容が国ごとに大きく異なる実態が浮かび上がりました。 今回新たに実施した分析では、2026年のAZEC首脳会合・閣僚会合開催国であるフィリピンにスポットライトを当てました。 フィリピンにおけるAZEC：進捗は限定的だが、潜在力を成果につなげられるか 2026年のAZEC首脳会合・閣僚会合開催国であるフィリピンは、AZEC関連協定の件数が5番目に多く、2023年から2025年の間に33件の協定を発表しました。同国は再生可能エネルギーや電力系統の刷新・最適化をはじめとする日本の技術にしばしば高い関心を寄せており、その技術が輸入化石燃料への依存度を低減し、エネルギー安全保障を強化するための鍵になると見込んでいます。 フィリピンのエネルギー計画では、2050年までに、発電容量における新規追加分のうち80％以上を再エネで賄うことを目指しており、エネルギー危機への対応策として再エネ開発が急ピッチで進められています。また、クリーンエネルギー導入を加速させたシナリオも現在策定中です。一方で、当団体の分析によれば、クリーンエネルギー分野における同国のAZEC関連協定はごくわずかに留まっています。 これまでのところ、AZECを通じて日本とフィリピンが締結した覚書（MOU）33件のうち、大半は農業と土地利用に重点を置いています。再エネを主な対象とするMOUはわずか2件で、具体的な再エネ発電プロジェクトに関するものはそのうち1件にとどまります。ただし、この1件は、東南アジアでも有数の規模を誇る陸上風力発電プロジェクトに数えられる重要なもので、現時点では103.5MWの出力が計画されています。そしてもう1件は、今後の再エネプロジェクトの資金調達の検討するものです。 出所：AZECを通じてフィリピンが締結したMOUの協力分野の内訳。2023年から2025年にかけて日本とフィリピンが締結・公表したAZEC関連のMOUをE3Gが分析。…

items.title: Diversity and spatial segregation of TRP channels in the closest relatives of animals
items.summary_raw: Sensory systems, built around specialized cell types, are central to how animals perceive and respond to their environments. However, the evolutionary origin of these systems remains unclear. Here, we show that choanoflagellates, the sister group of animals, possess remarkably diverse repertoires of transient receptor potential (TRP) channels, an ancient superfamily of sensory ion channels. Comparative analyses indicate that most major animal TRP channel families predate the origin of animals and reveal extensive radiations of the TRPM and TRPW families within choanoflagellates, with the latter family likely being lost in the animal lineage. Furthermore, in the choanoflagellate model Salpingoeca rosetta , TRPA, TRPC and TRPV occupy discrete microdomains within the collar complex, a key interface for environmental sensing and feeding. We propose that the evolution of animal sensory systems involved both expansion and reorganization of this ancestral repertoire, with subcellular patterning in unicellular organisms representing a precursor to cell-type specialization in multicellular animals.

items.title: Density-dependent aggregation underlies spatial self-organization in coastal dunes
items.summary_raw: Across coastal ecosystems, habitat-forming organisms interact with wind and water to generate biogeomorphic feedbacks that produce spatially patterned landscapes. Such spatial patterns can emerge through different self-organizing mechanisms, with contrasting implications for ecosystem resilience. Here, we test whether spatial dynamics in developing coastal dunes are better explained by scale-dependent feedback or by density-dependent aggregation (DDA), the latter being a more recently proposed mechanism of spatial self-organization. Using high-resolution aerial imagery and coupled time series of elevation, we tracked the spatial dynamics of dune-grass patches and sand accumulation during early dune development. Rather than converging toward a dominant size or spacing, both dune-grass patches and the dune bodies they collectively form coarsened through time, with self-similar size distributions shifting toward larger scales. Sand accumulation was disproportionately concentrated in already-dense vegetation, with a density–growth relationship that changes sign at a critical threshold. Together, these findings are consistent with DDA rather than scale-dependent feedback as the dominant mechanism of spatial self-organization in developing coastal dunes. The resulting density–growth relationship implies threshold-dependent resilience to local disturbances. Once local vegetation density falls below a critical point, decline is self-reinforcing rather than self-dampening, with…

items.title: Trans - and cis -interaction dynamics of cadherin complexes on membranes visualized by high-speed atomic force microscopy
items.summary_raw: Classical cadherin-mediated cell–cell adhesion is important for maintaining the animal body and defects in adhesion cause severe diseases. The combination of trans - (between cells) and cis - (on the same membrane) interactions of the extracellular domains of cadherins is necessary for cadherin clustering in cell–cell junctions, which is essential for robust tissue formation. However, the solution structure and interaction dynamics of trans / cis -binding cadherin complexes have not been observed because of technical limitations; therefore, the cadherin clustering mechanism is not well understood. In this study, we reconstituted trans / cis -binding cadherin complexes on membranes and visualized their structure and dynamics using high-speed atomic force microscopy. Our method revealed trans -strand-swap interactions through flipping and hopping motions and cis -interactions, which contributed to multiple interaction patterns on the membrane. In addition, we observed cadherin complex structures that were distinct from those in crystal structures. These results suggest that cadherins adopt dynamic and diverse conformations through multiple assembly pathways on the membrane.

items.title: Enhancement of hippocampal synaptic AMPA receptor function by the antidepressant tianeptine and by opioid peptides
items.summary_raw: Management of major depressive disorder (MDD) with conventional therapeutics that enhance monoaminergic neurotransmission requires prolonged treatment prior to clinical benefit and a substantial proportion of patients show little or no improvement. Identifying alternative molecular targets is required to develop efficacious, rapid acting antidepressants. In this regard, tianeptine, an established but atypical clinical antidepressant, is of interest. Tianeptine does not directly influence monoamine levels; in rodents it has a relatively rapid onset of antidepressant-like efficacy and, unusually for an antidepressant, exhibits procognitive properties. Here, voltage-clamp recordings from mouse hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons demonstrated tianeptine enhanced the amplitude of neurally evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents mediated by glutamate activation of synaptic α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors (AMPARs). The effect required intracellular polyamines and expression of the GluA1 subunit. These observations suggest that tianeptine relieves the channel block by endogenous polyamines of synaptic GluA1 containing AMPARs (GluA1-AMPARs). The tianeptine effect was abolished by postsynaptic inhibition of G-protein signaling, was reduced in mice lacking either the µ- or the δ-opioid receptor, and inhibited by selective antagonists of these receptors, collectively demonstrating that the facilitation of excitatory transmission was indirectly mediated by…

items.title: MATRIN3 deficiency in human cells triggers an autoinflammatory response via cGAS–STING activation
items.summary_raw: MATRIN3 (MATR3) is a broadly expressed nuclear RNA-binding protein. However, the mechanisms by which MATR3 maintains human cellular health remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed gene editing to model MATR3 deficiency in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and the HAP1 haploid cell line. To investigate the consequences of MATR3 loss-of-function, we profiled gene expression changes by RNA sequencing, which revealed significant upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in MATR3-deficient cells, indicating activation of innate immune signaling. To elucidate the mechanism underlying ISG upregulation, we identified direct targets of MATR3 using photoactivatable ribonucleoside-enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (PAR-CLIP). In one of these targets, TDRD3 , a gene required for R-loop metabolism in conjunction with Topoisomerase III Beta ( TOP3B ), MATR3 loss induced the incorporation of a 53-nucleotide-long poison exon that triggered nonsense-mediated decay and subsequent reduction in its expression. Consistent with dysfunction of the TDRD3–TOP3B complex, MATR3 loss led to the aberrant accumulation of cytoplasmic RNA–DNA hybrids, which activated the inflammatory cGAS–STING pathway. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized role of MATR3 in maintaining RNA processing fidelity and cellular homeostasis, and establish a mechanistic link between MATR3 dysfunction and innate immune activation. This molecular cascade has significant…

Hyperfunction of PSD-95 leads to hyperexcitability and cognitive abnormalities in MEF2C haploinsufficiency
items.summary_raw: Myocyte enhancer factor 2C (MEF2C) is a transcription factor critical for brain circuit development and cognitive behavior. The loss of one copy of MEF2C leads to MEF2C haploinsufficiency syndrome (MCHS), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, epilepsy, and behavioral phenotypes associated with autism spectrum disorders. Given that numerous genes are regulated by MEF2C, the neuronal and behavioral deficits in MCHS are complex, and there is currently no effective disease-modifying strategy for this disorder. Here, we show that MEF2C haploinsufficiency in forebrain excitability neurons led to an elevation of postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95) in mice. This elevation of PSD-95 coincided with an increased number of structural synapses, facilitated surface expression of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, augmented neuronal excitability, and increased susceptibility to seizures. Knocking down PSD-95 or inhibiting the interaction between PSD-95 and NMDA receptors efficiently reduced hyperexcitability phenotypes in MEF2C haploinsufficiency. Most importantly, knocking down PSD-95 significantly improved cognitive behaviors in mice with MEF2C haploinsufficiency. In summary, our study revealed a mechanism underlying hyperexcitability and cognitive defects associated with MCHS and suggests PSD-95 as a therapeutic target for MCHS.

items.title: Everyday adaptation in a gilded trap: Risk-taking and resilience in Maine’s lobster fishery
items.summary_raw: Flexibility is widely regarded as an enabling factor of adaptive capacity among natural resource users. Yet, as ecological systems around the world become increasingly simplified and social environments reduce diversification options, flexibility is becoming limited. Despite this trend, efforts to study how people adapt within the confines of constrained social–ecological systems have been sparse. Here, we broaden the analysis of resilience through a study of the American lobster fishery in Maine, United States, one of the most valuable fisheries in the world. Drawing on 307,000 observations from 3,515 harvesters over a 13-y period (2010–2022), we used a generalized linear mixed-effects model to analyze how sociodemographic characteristics, economic conditions, and time shape the probability of fishing during poor weather conditions, which we define as high-risk. We find demographic and socioeconomic heterogeneity in risk-taking: Men, mid-career harvesters, and captains of larger businesses were more likely to fish in risky conditions, and both low landings and high catch prices increased risk-taking. Contrary to our prediction, however, we observed an overall decline in risk-taking through time. We argue that harvesters instead relied on everyday adaptation—individual-scale, short- and medium-term adjustments in business strategy that occur within the constraints of the existing social–ecological system—to maintain resilience without increasing risk. Observable shifts in…

items.title: Bioinspired negative-curvature monomer architecture accelerates on-surface topochemical polymerization
items.summary_raw: On-surface chemical reactions are often limited by competing requirements for long range molecular order and the local atomic scale dynamics needed for bond formation. In many topochemical reactions, including diacetylene photopolymerization, alkyl-chain ordering provides the required geometric registry but can also restrict the conformational motion necessary for efficient reaction. Here, we show that bioinspired phospholipid architectures accelerate topochemical polymerization at interfaces by introducing multiple, distinct forms of packing frustration that operate on both molecular and nanoscopic scales. Diacetylene phosphocholines (dPCs) and phosphoethanolamines (dPEs), when confined to striped lamellar morphologies on graphitic substrates, undergo substantially faster on-surface photopolymerization than structurally analogous 10,12-tricosadiynoic acid (TCDA) monolayers (t 1/2 ~ 36 min for TCDA, 26 min for dPC, and 3 min for dPE). Molecular dynamics simulations show that topological constraints imposed by the glycerol linkage reduce alkyl-chain segmental order in both phospholipids, increasing the frequency of short separation distances between bond-forming carbons required for reaction. For dPE, typically considered a negative-curvature phospholipid, confinement to a lamellar geometry also frustrates directional headgroup hydrogen bond networks, further increasing reactivity. Together, these results identify complementary mechanisms by which topologically constrained…

items.title: Global grassland productivity and carbon storage benefit from functional diversity under climate change
items.summary_raw: Functional diversity plays an important role for ecosystem services of managed grasslands such as their gross primary productivity (GPP) and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. Yet vegetation models assessing functional diversity have been limited to small spatial scales. We used the Lund-Potsdam-Jena managed land (LPJmL) competitor stress-tolerant ruderal (CSR) model to assess the role of functional diversity for managed grassland GPP and SOC under climate change at the global scale. LPJmL-CSR simulates functional diversity using plant functional types representing different ecological strategies based on functional traits connected to CSR strategies. Our simulation experiments assumed low and high functional diversity levels and moderate and strong climate change scenarios. Results show that functional diversity plays an important role for GPP and SOC stocks already under moderate climate change. Strong loss of functional diversity prohibits communities’ adaptation to climate change, resulting in loss of GPP and SOC. Spatial patterns of GPP and SOC stocks show substantial differences between the low and high functional diversity scenarios dependent on regional conditions. These results are consistent with empirical findings and support the importance of functional diversity as insurance against climate change. The results of our global-scale model assessment show that enhancing functional diversity could be crucial for maintaining grassland productivity and thus human…

items.title: Cell jamming transition is regulated by mitochondrial pyruvate transport and endocytosis
items.summary_raw: Epithelial tissues undergo dynamic transitions between fluid-like collective motion and mechanically jammed states during development, injury repair, and disease progression. However, the cellular programs that drive these transitions and regulate collective behavior remain unclear. Using a controlled crowding model integrated with live-cell imaging and time-resolved multiomics, we demonstrate that epithelial crowding triggers early metabolic changes characterized by increased mitochondrial pyruvate anaplerosis that precedes the jamming transition. Restricting mitochondrial pyruvate import increased collective cell motility and delayed jamming in crowded monolayers. This unjammed state is driven by enhanced cytoskeletal remodeling and requires RhoA-myosin II activity. Mechanistically, we show that elevated cytoskeletal signaling promotes macropinocytic uptake, which serves as a required feedback loop to maintain motility. These findings identify mitochondrial pyruvate utilization as an important regulatory input linking metabolic remodeling to the endocytic control of epithelial fluidity.

items.title: Infection of macrophages by mpox virus activates inflammasome and cell death, informing multitarget therapeutic strategies
items.summary_raw: Severe mpox virus (MPXV) infection causes immunopathological manifestations in patients. Here, we provide clinical evidence of MPXV-induced inflammation in a large patient cohort and demonstrate direct macrophage infection in skin tissues from an autopsied mpox patient. In human macrophages, MPXV efficiently enters, replicates, and produces infectious particles. Infection activates both AIM2 and NLRP3 inflammasomes, triggering inflammatory responses and three forms of programmed cell death: pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis. Inflammasome inhibition reduces MPXV-induced inflammation and cell death without affecting viral replication. Screening clinically used anti-inflammatory drugs identified flufenamic acid, which suppresses MPXV-induced inflammation and cell death and, unexpectedly, also inhibits viral infection. Combined treatment with flufenamic acid and the antiviral brincidofovir further enhances suppression of viral infection, inflammatory response, and cell death, while largely preventing MPXV-induced transcriptomic reprogramming in macrophages. These effects were consistent across clade IIb, Ia, and Ib strains associated with the 2022–2023 global and recent African outbreaks. Together, our findings provide insight into MPXV immunopathology and support multitarget therapeutic strategies for severe mpox.

items.title: Neutralization titers reveal the structure of polyclonal antibody responses
items.summary_raw: The composition of a polyclonal antibody response is hard to measure experimentally but contains vital information about the robustness of immunity. Here, we argue that the statistics of neutralization titers alone can be used to make quantitative predictions about the composition of the response, circumventing challenges arising through sequencing and monoclonal antibody expression. We show that the response against influenza within a cohort can be either driven by a collective phenomenon where many antibodies contribute to neutralization, or dominated by just a few strong binders, leading to a broad distribution of titers across individuals described by a Gumbel distribution from extreme value theory. Comparing titers across cohorts, we find that Gumbel statistics accurately describe individuals prior to an immune challenge. We propose an equilibrium binding model that quantitatively captures titer data and illustrates the structure of the polyclonal response. Our approach extends generically to immune responses to other pathogens.

items.title: Correction for Campana, The market for human smuggling: Structure, mechanisms, and paradoxes
Barry Bloom and the convergence of immunology, infectious disease, and public health
items.summary_raw: In early 2026, the world lost Barry Bloom, a great advocate for public health, an extraordinarily accomplished immunologist, and a science advisor who helped refocus policy on controlling infectious diseases, including neglected diseases such as leprosy. Barry’s career took him from a life of laboratory discovery where he was enormously influential in catalyzing the late 20th century shift from studying the immune response of simple molecules to pathogenic microbes. As Dean of Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health he had a profound influence on the growth of the institution and the careers of many who have continued his work.

items.title: Bone morphogenetic protein signaling as a key regulator of retinal fibrosis
items.summary_raw: Retinal fibrosis is a blinding complication of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and idiopathic epiretinal membrane (iERM), yet effective therapies remain lacking. The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of BMP2 and BMP4 (BMP2/4)–activin receptor-like kinase (ALK) signaling in retinal fibrosis. BMP2 was detected in the vitreous of PDR, PVR, and rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) samples at concentration of 70, 180, and 85 pg/mL respectively, whereas it was present only at trace levels or was undetectable in the vitreous of macular hole and idiopathic ERM samples (~0.1 pg/mL). PDR, PVR, and idiopathic ERMs exhibited strong immunoreactivity for BMP2, BMP4, ALK3 (Bmpr1a), pSMAD1/5/9, and pSMAD4. Formation of preretinal fibronectin-containing membranes resulted from intravitreal injection of wild-type mice with BMP2 and similar membranes formed in mice expressing constitutively active ALK3 (caBmpr1a). The presence of preretinal membrane in caBmpr1a was confirmed by optical coherence tomography. The limited hyperoxia-induced proliferative retinopathy (LIHPR) model demonstrated a progressive increase in the retinal expression of BMP2 and BMP4and development of preretinal membrane. Administration of BMP/ALK inhibitor LDN193189 induced regression of the preretinal membrane in LHIPR. items.title: Geometric criterion for capillary thread breakup in rectangular microchannels
items.summary_raw: Capillary breakup of fluid threads underlies lab-on-a-chip diagnostics, drug encapsulation, and oil trapping in underground rock. Rectangular channels are the practical norm, yet no unified geometric criterion explains how their shape controls the onset and geometry of breakup. Combining direct numerical simulations, stop-flow analysis, and static equilibrium analysis, we show that breakup is triggered when the family of equilibrium neck shapes terminates. The associated critical continuous-phase volume depends only on the channel aspect ratio W / H , and the critical neck geometry transitions between two distinct collapse modes at a threshold W / H ≈ 2.0 . Below this threshold, the neck detaches from the top and bottom walls before pinch-off, with a slow three-dimensional necking stage intervening between the two events. Above it, detachment and pinch-off coincide. This geometry-derived critical volume serves as the mechanism-based input to a semiempirical thread-length model, validated for both primary thread breakup and secondary thread breakup across W / H from 1.0 to 3.0. Turning this principle into a design rule, we design a curved junction that matches the critical neck profile and directly reduces the critical volume, enabling on-chip production of densely packed emulsions beyond the close-packing limit of monodisperse spheres. By linking confined thread breakup in rectangular microchannels to a single dimensionless ratio, these results provide geometry-based design…

items.title: Myeloid cell reprogramming drives enhanced defense against Streptococcus pneumoniae lung infection following exposure to commensal Prevotella
items.summary_raw: Clinical data link the prevalent respiratory tract anaerobe Prevotella with reduced pneumonia mortality, but the mechanisms directing Prevotella regulation of lung immune homeostasis are unclear. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to define the transcriptional immune signatures underlying improved clearance of Streptococcus pneumoniae following lung exposure to Prevotella melaninogenica . Overall, we observed a substantial shift in myeloid cell transcriptional programming from interferon-dominant to a more antibacterial profile in S. pneumoniae –infected mice after pre-exposure to P. melaninogenica , correlating with increased macrophage and neutrophil phagocytosis of S. pneumoniae and improved pathogen clearance. In neutrophils, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling through TNFR2 was essential for increased antimicrobial function. Moreover, improved defense required CCR2-dependent monocyte-derived macrophages, with selective enrichment of more a mature Cxcl3+ population which was distinct from the hallmark S. pneumoniae –associated C1qa+ population enriched in the absence of effective clearance. Together, these findings inform the myeloid cell transcriptional changes associated with natural infection resistance mediated by pulmonary microbial exposures.

Our guest today is in charge of navigating those opposing trends and figuring out what comes next. Kurt Kelty started his career at Panasonic in 1993, where he led the company’s battery research lab. items.summary_raw: There are many markers of fall: vibrant foliage, apple picking, and pumpkin-spiced everything, to name a few. Cranking up the heat is another. With record-setting energy prices, everyone is bracing for higher bills. For the more than 4 million households that rely on heating oil, this winter could be particularly devastating. The war with Iran has pushed the cost of heating oil, which is essentially diesel, higher than it ever has been. It is hovering around $6 a gallon across much of the Northeast, where about 82 percent of homes that burn the fuel are located. That’s compared to the mid-$3 range in February. The National Energy Assistance Directors Association , or NEADA, projects that the cost of warming a home with that fossil fuel will go up 50 percent across those states. That amounts to $878 per household, or some $3.8 billion overall. “The volatility of this product right before winter is scary,” said Mark Wolfe, executive director of the organization, which had projected a lower increase just weeks earlier . “This is part of the cost of the war.” The stalemate in the Mideast has curtailed ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a tenth of the world’s water-borne diesel once flowed. Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, another major source of diesel, have further curbed the global supply. items.title: The never-ending struggle to protect Georgia’s most popular beach
items.summary_raw: Barrier islands like Tybee Island, off the coast of Georgia, should naturally accumulate sand from islands farther north, but human activity — development on the island, building sea walls and jetties, creating shipping channels — has disrupted that process. As a result, barrier islands are constantly losing sand, and the beaches are constantly being washed away by the relentless tide. To address the problem, the Army Corps of Engineers has, since the 1970s, been dredging up sand and depositing it onto beaches up and down the east coast. On Tybee, which sits just south of the mouth of the Savannah River, beach renourishment happens every seven years. The natural sand-sharing there is further interrupted by the shipping channel that cuts between Tybee and its neighbors to the north. In the winter of 2019 and 2020, the Corps placed 1.3 million cubic yards of sand on the Tybee Island beach. More than half of that sand is gone now. On one stretch near the DeSoto Beach Hotel, the dune looks like it’s been chopped in half with a giant knife, ending in a 5-foot cliff instead of a gradual slope. “It’s extremely stark and startling to see up close and personal,” said city manager Bret Bell. “You can see the vegetation. It’s bisected in half. You can see the roots coming out of the dune system.” It’s not just the dune grasses. In some places, the tide and storms have cut into sea turtle nests buried in the dune. Cílem ITS je zefektivnění využívání elektrizační soustavy. Nezbytné je posílit adresnost úhrad za službu distribuční soustavy tak, aby více odpovídaly skutečně vyvolaným nákladům. Od ledna proto dojde ke zpoplatnění rezervovaného příkonu u odběratelů na hladinách VN a VVN. Změna zákazníky motivuje k tomu, aby uvolnili rezervovaný příkon, který dlouhodobě nevyužívají, ale dosud za něj nemuseli platit, čímž se přenášely náklady na ostatní odběratele. Změny tarifní struktury tak uvolní kapacity pro nové žadatele o připojení a zároveň umožní využívání a rozvoj nových technologií. „Soustavu musíme využívat efektivně. Jedině tak můžeme investice související s transformací celé energetiky minimalizovat a nasměrovat tam, kde jsou…

items.title: IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings: Debt, energy and climate crises loom large
items.summary_raw: Just weeks after devastating floods hit Bangkok, the city will host the world’s finance leaders for the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings (12–18 October). Delegates will confront a global economy under pressure from fossil fuel supply shocks, rising debt distress and accelerating climate impacts, with many economies facing constrained fiscal space, including in Asia. The meetings, […]

items.title: Redefining fuel poverty: Introducing the temporal equity framework (TEF)
Techno-optimistic scientists take fewer climate actions
items.summary_raw: Abstract Technological innovation is key to mitigating climate change, yet excessive faith in technology may undermine the wider societal transformations needed to address it. In their roles as knowledge producers and trusted public figures, scientists play an important part in shaping how societies understand and respond to climate change. We examine techno-optimism—here defined as the belief that technology will largely solve the problems caused by climate change—among scientists using survey data from N = 9199 scientists across 115 countries. Our findings show that techno-optimism is most prevalent among scientists in applied and natural sciences, and among those with right-leaning political views, but does not vary with the extent to which one’s research is related to climate change. Techno-optimistic scientists are substantially less likely to engage in civic climate action (23% lower) or make high-impact lifestyle changes (18% lower). We hope that our study can contribute to a critical discussion about how scientists’ own beliefs and worldviews shape their understanding of, and engagement in, climate action.

items.title: Diverse coupling between climate change, socio-economic factors and climate potential productivity in Africa
items.summary_raw: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP and its driving mechanisms has therefore become an urgent research priority. This study analyses the spatiotemporal patterns and correlates of CPP across Africa, using the Thornthwaite Memorial model in combination with trend detection, correlation, and econometric analyses. The results reveal a declining CPP trend over 1901–2019, with a distinct latitudinal zonal distribution. CPP is highly sensitive to both temperature and precipitation. Continued deterioration is a likely consequence of future warmer and drier conditions. During 2000–2019, the predictive associations between CPP and industrialization, energy consumption, and PM2.5 emissions are directionally heterogeneous. CPP exhibits a unidirectional association with industrialization and PM2.5 emissions, while maintaining a bidirectional association with energy consumption. The industrialization‑CPP relationship follows an environmental Kuznets curve pattern, while CPP correlates positively with energy consumption and weakly negatively with PM2.5. These findings provide a scientific basis for understanding the dynamic evolution of Africa’s CPP and the socio‑ecological factors, and offer quantitative insights into the trade‑offs and synergies among environmental health, climate…

items.title: Unpacking climate justice rhetoric: a comparative content analysis of international city networks
items.summary_raw: Purpose The rising membership and influence of international city networks have positioned cities as important actors in global policy debates on climate change and sustainability. This study aims to clarify how these networks frame and incorporate justice in their climate actions. Design/methodology/approach The study selected four prominent city networks (C40, CityNet, ICLEI and UCLG) and applied a content analysis method to examine how they interpret justice in 64 documents published by them between 2016 and 2022. The documents were analysed from three perspectives: 1) usage of justice terminology, 2) justice dimensions (distributive, participatory or recognition justice); and 3) the contexts. Findings The study found that the framing of justice varied according to the missions and worldviews of the networks. However, except for CityNet, an increased consideration of justice was observed across the networks since the late 2010s. Notably, C40 increasingly emphasised climate justice in its documentation, despite being criticised for its neoliberal orientation towards urban climate policy. Conversely, CityNet, a regional city network of the Asia-Pacific, showed limited usage of justice terminology. Originality/value The findings suggest that justice framings in international city networks carry important implications for urban climate governance by shaping how justice is interpreted and prioritised in climate actions. However, concerns also arise that city networks may…

items.title: Agricultural blockchain readiness environment and carbon emission intensity in maize production: evidence from provincial panel data in major maize-producing areas of China
items.summary_raw: China’s major maize-producing regions face the joint challenge of sustaining food production and reducing agricultural emissions. Existing research on digital agriculture often uses broad digitalization measures and therefore does not distinguish the regional conditions that may enable information management, traceability, and verification applications associated with blockchain. This study constructs an Agricultural Blockchain Readiness Environment Index (ABRE Index, block_index) using entropy weighting across digital infrastructure, the agricultural industrial base, and policy support. The index measures regional readiness and enabling conditions rather than realized blockchain adoption. Using 180 province-year observations for 12 major maize-producing provinces from 2010 to 2024, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models with province-clustered inference and conduct supplementary robustness analyses. The ABRE Index is negatively associated with carbon emissions per unit of maize-sown area, with the baseline coefficient statistically significant at the 10% level under conventional clustered inference and supported by supplementary inference procedures. The coefficient remains negative in all 12 leave-one-out specifications, is statistically significant at the 10% level or better in 10 specifications, and the wild cluster bootstrap test yields p = 0.0415. The index is positively correlated with blockchain-related patent activity ( r = 0.1883, p = 0.0114), although this…

items.title: Legitimizing nuclear power: Rhetoric, myth and symbols in South Korea's official nuclear communication, 1986–2016
items.summary_raw: Understanding how nuclear power is justified matters for debates over energy security and climate change. Yet research has paid limited attention to how language, narratives, and images work together to sustain these justifications over time. This article examines South Korea's official nuclear communication from 1986 to 2016 through interpretive document analysis. It analyzes government and industry publications, educational materials, advertisements, sponsored journalism, and visual campaigns using rhetoric, myth, and symbol as analytical categories. Naming and euphemism downplayed risk in official accounts. Repeated narratives presented nuclear power as safe, affordable, indispensable, and environmentally responsible. Visual symbols associated it with scientific control and everyday life. These justifications persisted through adaptation. Major accidents were reframed as problems of technical management, while environmental claims were incorporated into established narratives of national development. Repeated circulation through education, advertising, and sponsored media formed a communication infrastructure that presented nuclear power as a normal and desirable national choice. The study examines the construction and circulation of these representations; it does not establish their causal effects on public acceptance or policy continuity. It advances energy communication research by showing how rhetorical adjustment, symbolic selection, and institutional repetition…

items.title: Framing of nationalism in climate reporting in the Global South: The case of India
items.summary_raw: Climate change and nationalism have traditionally been viewed as opposing forces because nationalism is often territorially bounded, while climate change transcends borders. This study examines the intersection of climate reporting and three forms of nationalism – that is, economic, resource and green nationalism – in India by analysing the coverage of Conference of the Parties (COP) summits in The Hindu and The Times of India before and after the Narendra Modi government’s rise in 2014. The findings show a shift from economic nationalism to green nationalism during the Modi regime, supported by the frames of leadership, sustainability and cultural superiority. Simultaneously, resource nationalism remained strong, highlighting the tensions emerging out of development priorities and climate action.

items.title: Making sense of loss and damage at the national level
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02768-w Climate change is already causing widespread losses and damages, and these impacts will intensify as human and natural systems exceed their capacity to adapt. Recent research allows us to understand if and how countries are prioritizing this issue in national policies.

items.title: Climate policy uncertainty, renewable energy transition, and sustainable economic development: Evidence from Türkiye using the Fourier-Augmented ARDL and TVP-VAR models
items.summary_raw: The transition toward renewable energy is a pillar of sustainable development and energy security strategies. However, climate policy uncertainty (CPU) may generate ambiguous investment signals, either discouraging or stimulating renewable energy development depending on institutional quality and market conditions. Although research on uncertainty and energy transition has expanded, evidence from emerging economies remains limited, particularly regarding the evolution of CPU effects over time. This study examines the short- and long-run impacts of climate policy uncertainty on renewable energy demand in Türkiye using quarterly data from 1990Q1 to 2025Q1. A Fourier-Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (FARDL) model identifies long-run equilibrium relationships while accounting for structural changes, whereas a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) model captures changes in dynamic responses. The findings show that climate policy uncertainty has a positive and statistically significant long-run effect on renewable energy demand. By contrast, short-run results indicate temporary negative responses to uncertainty shocks, suggesting that policy uncertainty initially delays renewable energy investment. TVP-VAR impulse responses reveal that the effect of CPU varies over time. Earlier periods display weak or negative responses, while recent years show stronger and more persistent positive effects, indicating that Türkiye’s renewable energy sector has become…

items.title: Impact of Climate-Smart Agricultural Education on Youth Livelihood in Bayelsa Riverine Communities
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE
items.summary_raw: This study evaluated the impact of climate-smart agricultural education on youth livelihoods across riverine communities in Bayelsa State. Guided by three research questions and three null hypotheses, the author adopted a mixed-method design integrating a cross-sectional descriptive survey with a quasi-experimental field trial. The target population consisted of active farming youths within Ekeremor and Southern Ijaw Local Government Areas. From this frame, the Taro Yamane formula determined a descriptive survey sample of 195 youths, while a nested cohort of 60 youths was purposively selected and split evenly into experimental and control groups (n=30 each) for experimental tracking. Data collection relied on the verified Youth Climate-Smart Agriculture and Livelihood Questionnaire and the objective Climate-Smart Agriculture Competency Assessment Test. Descriptive questions were analyzed using mean and standard deviation, whereas the null hypotheses were tested via Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) at a 0.05 level of significance. The empirical findings demonstrated that targeted education in flood resilient crop production, advanced fish farming, and aquaponics significantly boosted practical vocational competencies, prompting the rejection of all three null hypotheses. The study concluded that institutionalized climate-smart agricultural training enhances economic resilience and promotes livelihood diversification in ecological flood zones, recommending that relevant state…

items.title: Impacts of Climate Hazards, Vulnerabilities, and Adaptation Strategies of Banana Producers in Senegal: A Scoping Review
items.source_name: African Journal of Climate and Resilience
items.summary_raw: Banana production in Senegal is vital for food security and rural income, yet it faces severe hydro-climatic disruptions across Tambacounda, Kolda, Sédhiou, and Saint-Louis. Utilizing an iterative literature search and thematic narrative synthesis, this study examines how scientific research characterizes climate influences on these agrosystems. Findings indicate that structural water deficits, river-surge flooding, and high winds diminish both productivity and commercial quality. Smallholder vulnerability is multidimensional, driven by low self-financing capacities and lowland exposure. Although producers employ adaptation techniques such as propping, mulching, and canal construction backed by state and NGO initiatives, stakeholder surveys frequently reveal these measures are inadequate against extreme weather intensity. To address these gaps, future research and public policy must prioritize local dynamic microclimatology to transcend macro-climatic scales and advance the statistical prediction of short-duration extreme events.

items.title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture
REScoops acting as intermediaries, influencing the scaling of energy communities; a multi-case analysis of five pilots in Europe
items.summary_raw: There is increasing scholarly attention to the scaling of energy communities (EC). Intermediaries have an important role here. Energy communities themselves, especially in the form of renewable energy cooperatives (REScoops), can take on this role very well. This paper addresses the question how REScoops, acting as intermediaries, influence the scaling of ECs. A longitudinal multi-case research design is adopted to answer this question. Five cases of EC pilots in different EU countries receiving intermediary support from REScoops were selected and researched over a three-year period. Data collection involved interviews, text documents, a quantitative longitudinal survey, and pilot project data. Results show that EC organisations use various forms of scaling: scaling-up, -out, and -deep. Regarding REScoops acting as an intermediary influencing the scaling of ECs, the analysis presents moderate support for positive impact. The relationship appears positive for scaling-deep and fairly positive for scaling-out. For scaling-up the relationship there was mostly within-case evidence. Scaling-up appears related to contextual factors. A fairly challenging context seems correlated to ECs deploying scaling-up strategies, using REScoop intermediary agency with the aim of changing key institutional structures, regulatory and policy frameworks that have a negative impact on ECs. This paper ends with suggestions for future work.

items.title: El comprometido proyecto de ampliación del Guggenheim de Bilbao. Una propuesta política rebatida socialmente
items.source_name: PH. Boletín del Instituto Andaluza del Patrimonio Histórico/PH/PH. Boletín del Instituto Andaluz del Patrimonio Histórico/Boletín informativo - Instituto Andaluz del Patrimonio Histórico
items.summary_raw: El proyecto de ampliación del Museo Guggenheim Bilbao planteaba la creación de una nueva sede en Urdaibai, espacio declarado por la Unesco como Reserva de la Biosfera. La propuesta se presentó como una oportunidad para regenerar económicamente la comarca y diversificar su oferta cultural bajo criterios de sostenibilidad ambiental, social y económica. Sin embargo, la ubicación elegida, un espacio natural protegido, generó una fuerte controversia social, política y mediática. El análisis del proyecto desde las cuatro dimensiones de la sostenibilidad (ambiental, económica, social y cultural) evidenció importantes tensiones. Organizaciones ecologistas y parte de la comunidad científica alertaron del impacto ecológico y de la reducción de la protección del dominio público marítimo-terrestre. Paralelamente, surgieron plataformas ciudadanas bajo el lema “Urdaibai ez dago salgai” (Urdaibai no se vende), denunciando un modelo de desarrollo percibido como impuesto y poco adaptado a las necesidades locales. El proceso de escucha impulsado por el Centro Lehendakari Agirre reveló cinco patrones de opinión social, destacando una mayoría crítica con la ampliación, pero favorable a nuevas inversiones que respetaran el entorno y respondieran a las demandas comarcales. Finalmente, en diciembre de 2025, las instituciones decidieron cancelar el proyecto. El caso muestra cómo la sostenibilidad requiere participación ciudadana efectiva, transparencia informativa y coherencia entre discurso…

items.title: Intersectional Framing Strategies by and for Indigenous Youth in Climate Governance
items.summary_raw: This article examines the role of Indigenous Youth in climate governance through intersectional frames to show how actors strategically construct themselves or are constructed by others as holding multiple identities simultaneously. Building on scholarship on climate governance, framing, and intersectionality, we ask how Indigenous Youth are positioned within climate debates and how they strategically represent themselves. The article draws on frame analysis of discursive materials from various climate, youth and Indigenous-themed actors in climate governance and on participant observation at the 2024 United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues. We argue that intersectionality is not only an analytical lens for identifying layered exclusion, but also a political framing strategy for inclusion and participation in climate governance. Our findings show important differences in how Indigenous Youth frame themselves, as vulnerable victims and/or empowered agents, compared to when they are framed by other actors. This research contributes to debates on climate governance by foregrounding Indigenous Youth as political actors and accentuating the stakes around their representation and participation in climate governance.

items.title: The Geography of Climate–Tourism Knowledge Production Across National Vulnerability–Exposure Profiles
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Climate–tourism research is often examined as a single, coherent body of knowledge. This study maps the geography of climate–tourism knowledge production and analyses whether its organisation varies according to the national contexts from which research is produced. To this end, the study adopts a contextual bibliometric approach and proposes a country classification based on vulnerability–exposure profiles, defined by the combination of climate vulnerability and tourism exposure. The 4585 articles indexed in Web of Science are linked to the countries of the authors' institutional affiliations, which allows knowledge organisation to be compared across four profiles through bibliographic coupling, co‐word analysis and journal outlet analysis. The results show that climate vulnerability is associated with two broad knowledge regimes: one centred on the sustainability and governance of tourism and the other oriented towards socio‐ecological vulnerability and adaptation. Tourism exposure modulates the scale at which climate‐related challenges are framed, ranging from destination management to broader socio‐ecological processes. Overall, the study shows that knowledge asymmetries are reflected not only in the volume of research output but also in how scientific knowledge is organised, consolidated and made visible.

items.title: From Demonstration to Commercialization: Global Trends in Advanced Biofuels with a Focus on Cellulosic Ethanol
items.summary_raw: Advanced biofuels are essential for decarbonizing transport sectors that are difficult to electrify, including aviation, shipping, and heavy-duty road transport. Since 2009, IEA Bioenergy Task 39 has monitored the global development of advanced biofuel technologies through an open-access database of pilot and demonstration facilities. The database provides systematically validated information on technology pathways, feedstocks, production capacities, operational status, and regional deployment trends. This work presents a long-term assessment of commercialization progress with a particular focus on cellulosic ethanol. The analysis shows that, despite strong early expectations, commercialization of cellulosic ethanol faced major barriers, including high production costs, technological complexity, feedstock logistics, and unstable policy support. More than 30 facilities were idled or closed after 2015. Nevertheless, recent developments indicate renewed momentum. By 2024, global operational capacity reached 556,000 t/a, with significant additional capacities under construction and planning. Brazil emerged as the leading growth market through integration with existing sugarcane and ethanol infrastructure, while China rapidly expanded capacity since 2018. The study highlights the critical role of demonstration plants, policy support, and international collaboration in scaling advanced biofuels and advancing sustainable low-carbon transport systems.

items.title: Market Readiness for Advanced Aviation and Shipping Fuels in Europe
items.summary_raw: Achieving the EU’s 2050 climate-neutrality target faces significant challenges in aviation and maritime transport. This study, conducted under the Horizon Europe BioTheRoS project, presents a PESTEL analysis of advanced sustainable fuels derived from pyrolysis and gasification across Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Spain, and Greece. Using a mixed-methods approach combining policy reviews, comparative country assessment, and quantitative and qualitative indicators, the research identifies political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal factors shaping market readiness levels in various geographical/regional landscapes. Results highlight strong political commitment and environmental drivers, contrasted with economic and legal barriers that limit large-scale deployment. Technological maturity and public acceptance vary across regions, while economic feasibility remains a critical constraint. The study emphasizes the need for coordinated policies, investment risk-sharing, harmonized regulations, and stakeholder engagement to accelerate adoption of advanced fuels. Findings support evidence-based policymaking, guide industry investment, and inform cross-border cooperation to advance Europe’s climate-neutrality objectives.

items.title: Češi se bojí zdražování a války. V krizích spoléhají na stát
МЕДІЙНІ ТЕХНІКИ КОНСТРУЮВАННЯ НАРАТИВІВ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ
items.source_name: Naukovì zapiski Nacìonalʹnogo unìversitetu «Ostrozʹka akademìâ» Serìâ «Fìlologìâ»
items.summary_raw: The article examines manipulative media techniques used to construct sustainability narratives in English-language media discourse. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing role of digital media and social networking platforms in shaping public perceptions of environmental issues, climate change, and sustainable development goals. The theoretical framework of the study is based on Critical Discourse Analysis approaches and the classification of media manipulative techniques proposed by Da San Martino et al. (2019). The research corpus consists of 100 publications from leading English-language media outlets (BBC, The Guardian, National Geographic, Greenpeace International, The New York Times, UN Environment Programme) and their corresponding Facebook and X accounts for the years 2025-2026. The methodology combines qualitative and quantitative content analysis with elements of Critical Discourse Analysis, enabling the identification of the frequency and functioning of media manipulative techniques. The results reveal the dominance of emotional-evaluative strategies of influence, particularly exaggeration/minimization, appeals to fear, and the use of emotionally charged vocabulary. It is established that different media exhibit distinct models of discursive behavior: Greenpeace International is characterized by a high level of emotional mobilization, whereas the BBC, The New York Times, and National Geographic combine emotional and fact-based strategies. The…

items.title: Sustainable energy transition options for Russia
items.summary_raw: Following the Paris Agreement, one way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and minimise the consequences of climate change is to pursue the goal of a sustainable energy supply by renewable energy sources. This study explores transition pathways towards sustainable energy system in the regions of Russia. Potential scenarios are presented in the power, heat, transport, and industry sectors. The study leverages an energy-industry system transition model in hourly resolution to investigate various policy scenarios ranging from 100% renewable energy in 2050 to net-zero emissions by 2060 with higher shares of nuclear power, to explore the feasibility and economic implications of the transition to a carbon-neutral energy system. The results show that respective transition pathways are technically feasible and economically viable. The analysis reveals that achieving zero CO 2 emissions by 2050 with very high renewable energy shares composed of wind power (56%), solar photovoltaics (40%), hydropower (3%), and bioenergy (1%) along with the deployment of power-to-X technologies is the lowest cost solution with cumulative CO 2 emissions around 22,000 MtCO 2 until 2060. The study underscores the importance of robust policy support and infrastructure development to facilitate this transition as a basis for economic development driven by low-cost and sustainable energy solutions.

items.title: Global warming and the National Cattlemen’s Association 1986–1996
items.summary_raw: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. This knowledge expanded views of responsibility for global warming beyond the fossil fuel sector. Using scientific studies, archival documents, media interviews, and various government reports, we analyzed how the National Cattlemen’s Association (NCA), a trade association for the U.S beef industry, reacted to news about its products’ impacts on global warming between 1986 and 1996. While previous studies have emphasized the role of trade associations in political lobbying, here we show that NCA responded mainly with strategic communications, including information gathering on civil society activities, commissioning academic experts to produce and share statistics that reframed scientific findings, and discursive tactics to influence politicians and the public. Despite scientific recommendations about opportunities to reduce methane emissions, we found no evidence that NCA researched or promoted any of these suggested changes to beef production. Instead, NCA treated global warming as a public relations concern that could affect consumer demand, rather than as a potentially serious consequence of beef production.

items.title: Digital twins for energy wells through multiscale physics-data fusion: Review, challenges, and a conceptual framework
items.summary_raw: Energy wells underpin critical technologies in the global energy transition, including geothermal energy extraction, carbon capture and storage, and underground hydrogen storage. In recent years, digital twin (DT) concepts have been increasingly explored to support well design, monitoring, and integrity management. However, most existing DT implementations for energy wells remain limited in scope and maturity, with incomplete integration of multiscale physics, evolving field data, and adaptive operational decision support. These limitations arise from heavy reliance on high-fidelity physics-based simulations with prohibitive computational costs, or on purely data-driven models that exhibit limited generalizability under evolving geological and operational conditions. To clarify the current state of the field, this paper first reviews recent DT developments for energy wells across oil and gas, geothermal, and subsurface energy storage applications. Building on this, we further synthesize advances in molecular dynamics, pore-scale simulation, continuum-scale thermo–hydro–mechanical–chemical modeling, and physics-informed machine learning, highlighting how multiscale physical processes governing clay–cement–fluid interactions, deformation, damage, and transport are currently treated in isolation. Motivated by these gaps, we propose a conceptual multiscale physics–data fusion DT framework for energy wells. The framework outlines an integrated architecture in which molecular- and…

items.title: ASSESSING THE FACTORS INFLUENCING PRIVATE VEHICLE OWNERS’ INTENTION TO PAY PROPOSED CONGESTION FEES IN GEORGE TOWN, PENANG: A THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOUR
items.summary_raw: Penang was identified as the most congested city in Malaysia in 2024, primarily due to the influx of tourists in George Town, which contributed to high greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the Penang State government proposed becoming the first state to implement a congestion fee. However, limited information was available regarding the stakeholders’ intentions towards congestion fees. Accordingly, the research aimed to determine the relationship between attitude, subjective norms (SN), perceived behavioural control (PBC), and intention to pay a congestion fee. Questionnaires were utilised to collect responses from 440 respondents through stratified sampling in George Town, involving residents of Penang and domestic tourists. The results of multiple regression analysis indicated that the constructs of the Theory of Planned Behaviour (Attitude, SN, and PBC) had significant and positive relationships. These findings provided valuable insights for the State Government and the Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department in designing effective congestion fee implementation strategies, which were aligned with the National Transport Policy 2021-2030 and SDG11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

items.title: Who should pay for energy transition costs? Political ideology and distributive fairness in Alberta
items.summary_raw: Public support for energy transition does not necessarily imply agreement over how its costs and benefits should be distributed. As governments accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy, political conflict increasingly centers not on whether the transition should occur, but on whether its economic burdens and benefits are allocated fairly. This paper examines how left–right political ideology shapes perceptions of distributive fairness in Alberta's energy transition. Using original survey data from 1527 Alberta residents, multivariate regression models analyze four dimensions of distributive fairness: funding mechanisms, responsibility for transition costs, the regional distribution of costs, and the regional distribution of benefits. The findings show that political ideology exerts selective rather than universal effects. Ideological differences are strongest when policies explicitly redistribute economic costs or benefits, particularly through higher taxes on the oil and gas industry and the regional distribution of transition benefits. By contrast, other dimensions of distributive fairness are more consistently associated with household energy burden, local energy dependence, institutional confidence, climate concern, and broader political value orientations. These findings demonstrate that distributive fairness is a distinct and multidimensional aspect of public opinion, with different distributive questions activating different political and contextual…

items.title: Climate change communication, adaptation, and mitigation through the arts: a rapid scoping review
items.summary_raw: Introduction Climate crisis is inherently intersectional; it is a health crisis and a cultural crisis too. Creative and innovative approaches are essential to address the complex and unequal health and wellbeing impacts of human induced climate change. This rapid scoping review aimed to review, synthesise, and analyse empirical studies that implemented arts-based interventions to promote climate change communication, adaptation, and mitigation. Methods We used the methodological framework for scoping reviews set out by Arksey and O’Malley and systematically searched five major electronic databases using the PRISMA reporting guidelines. Results Sixteen studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this review. Programmes varied and included environmental art festivals, climate summits, ecological conferences, theater and open-air performances, exhibitions, musical events, fieldtrips, nature conservation and sustainability interventions. Most studies focused on climate change communication, using the arts to raise environmental awareness and translate public health messages more clearly and accessibly. Only four studies focused on climate change adaptation (e.g., arts for coping with climate emotions) and mitigation (e.g., arts for motivating cultural shifts towards low-carbon lifestyles and practices). Discussion Arts-based programmes focusing on climate change adaptation and mitigation are disproportionately low compared to climate change communication…

items.title: How communication fosters climate-related communicative self-efficacy among young people: insights from a pedagogical intervention in Climate Change Education
items.summary_raw: Climate Change Education increasingly emphasizes participation and agency alongside knowledge acquisition. Within this context, self-efficacy plays a central role, yet the relationship between communication and self-efficacy in climate education remains ­underexplored. To investigate this relationship empirically, a communication-based workshop entitled ‘Climate Talks: Speak Up – Cool Down!’ was conducted with 140 secondary school students aged 14–18 in Tyrol, Austria. The intervention followed a democratic, participatory, and dialogue-oriented approach and included reflection tasks, message development, peer discussions, and structured feedback processes. Data were collected through pre- and post-intervention questionnaires assessing general self-efficacy and climate communicative self-efficacy (CCSE). The findings show that students initially rated their CCSE significantly lower than their general self-efficacy. Following the intervention, CCSE increased significantly, indicating that communication-oriented educational settings can strengthen learners’ confidence in engaging with climate-related discussions. The study therefore highlights communication as a realistic and accessible domain in which young people can experience effectiveness and participation in relation to climate change.

items.title: Recognized but displaced: Uranium mill tailings and the sustainability accounting of nuclear energy
items.summary_raw: Nuclear-energy sustainability is usually debated through reactor performance, carbon intensity, fuel availability, operational safety and spent-fuel disposal. Less visible are the front-end residues generated by uranium production, especially uranium mill tailings (UMT), likely the nuclear fuel cycle's largest long-lived radioactive residue stream by volume. This Perspective argues that UMT are not merely neglected; they are recognized and displaced through nested governance boundaries. It develops the concept of volume-based leniency and identifies three linked mechanisms: classification displacement, infrastructural pragmatism and sustainability-accounting displacement. Historical regulation, current naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM) and remediation frameworks, the Wismut programme, written clarifications from Nordic radiation-safety authorities, and uranium-mining legacies show how competent institutions can each address a bounded part of the problem without assembling the long-term radioactive, chemical, ecological, financial and distributive liability as a whole. The resulting issue is not whether all tailings should be reclassified as conventional radioactive waste. It is whether nuclear-energy sustainability can be judged credibly when front-end liabilities remain outside, or only weakly attached to, the system boundary used to assess the electricity they enable. Whole-system accounting should not predetermine whether nuclear energy is sustainable; it…

items.title: Mobilising private finance for nature: learning from large-scale nature investment vehicles
items.summary_raw: This report analyses the structure and use of proceeds of 54 nature investment vehicles and sets out implications for policymakers, investors, fund managers and project developers.

items.title: Exclusive: Data Center Cancellations Top $260 Billion in 2026
items.summary_raw: The country’s largest technology companies are expected to spend more than $800 billion this year investing in data centers and artificial intelligence. But new data suggests the local backlash to data centers may be taking a meaningful bite out of that boom. At least $260 billion of data center investments were canceled this year after sustained local opposition, according to new Heatmap Pro data. The pace and size of those cancellations is picking up. About $130 billion in data center investment — or about half of the total — was canceled in the three months ending on September 30. And in dollar terms, the size of canceled projects in the third quarter of 2026 exceeded the size of all data center projects canceled last year. Roughly $1 trillion in data center investment now faces some kind of sustained or meaningful local opposition, according to Heatmap Pro data. About half of all projects that have met local backlash this year were ultimately canceled, our data suggests. Our market intelligence service Heatmap Pro tracks local projects and regulations affecting clean energy, batteries, and data centers. We run a continuous survey of public officials, regulatory filings, and local media to monitor energy and data center cancellations nationwide. Our investment figures, which have not been previously published and are larger than other estimates, are likely an undercount. Only about 60% of data center projects disclose the size of their planned investment, especially…
