items.title: A comparative analysis of climate adaptation and migration governance in Spain and Morocco
items.summary_raw: Examined in this paper is the relationship between environmental change and human mobility through a comparative analysis of Spain and Morocco. While Spain is often examined through the perspectives of European climate policy, decentralised governance, and demographic transformation, Morocco is studied in relation to climate vulnerability, water stress, rural development, and/or adaptation capacity. This study addresses the limited comparative attention given to how both countries govern the emerging links between climate change and mobility. Drawing on Adaptive Governance Theory, the research analyses the extent to which climate adaptation and migration policies coordinate and develop adaptive capacities. The analysis focuses on four governance dimensions: institutional coordination, policy integration, flexibility and adaptation, and multi-level governance. The findings indicate that the two cases have developed important environmental governance and migration management capacities; however, significant gaps remain in integrating climate and mobility frameworks. The study highlights three broader governance lessons: the need to recognise the social consequences of climate change, strengthen coordination across policy sectors and governance levels, and enhance knowledge production and stakeholder participation. The paper contributes to debates on climate mobility and demonstrates the importance of adaptive governance approaches in addressing complex socio-ecological…

items.title: Spatial perspective on perceived fairness of climate-related fuel tax increases
items.summary_raw: We explore the perceived fairness of fuel tax increases from a spatial perspective. Actions in transport sector are needed to meet climate change mitigation targets, but such policies may disproportionately impact rural and urban residents, leading to spatially varying experiences of injustice. Perceived fairness is the most important determinant of public opinion towards mitigation policies, but perceived fairness of these policies itself has been understudied. We combine our inquiry of perceived fairness regarding fuel tax increases with considerations of spatial justice. We explore, whether residential area type, region, and variables such as climate concern, trust in climate policies, political orientation and use of fossil-fuelled car, are associated with perceived fairness of increasing fuel tax, and whether there are regional differences in these variables. Data were collected via a survey in June 2022 in three regions with different characteristics in Finland: Helsinki, Finland Proper, and Northern Ostrobothnia. Our results reveal that residents in rural areas and sparsely populated regions perceive fuel tax increases as less fair. Climate concern, trust and political orientation were found to influence fairness perceptions. Moreover, climate concern and trust were lower in sparsely populated regions. Considerations of fairness perceptions are important for successful climate mitigation policy.

items.title: An Analysis of University Students’ Attitudes Toward Healthy Eating
items.summary_raw: This study aimed to examine the attitudes towards healthy eating among students of the Faculty of Sports Sciences at Mardin Artuklu University. The research was conducted using a survey model, a quantitative research method, and included a total of 315 university students (127 women and 188 men) who voluntarily participated. A personal information form and the Healthy Eating Attitude Scale were used as data collection tools. The data obtained were evaluated using independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson correlation analysis. According to the research findings, female students' scores were found to be higher than male students only in the “Poor Eating (KB)” sub-dimension. Regarding the age variable, it was determined that students aged 26 and over had lower total scores on the Knowledge About Nutrition (BHB), Positive Eating (OB), KB, and Healthy Eating Attitude Scale (SBITO) scales compared to younger groups. Regarding housing status, students living in dormitories had higher total SBITO scores than those living in family homes. Regarding class level, a significant difference was found only in the “BHB” sub-dimension; however, a significant difference was found in the “Feelings About Nutrition (BYD)” sub-dimension in the smoking variable. It was determined that students who did not engage in physical activity had higher “BYD” scores than those who did. In conclusion, it has been shown that university students' attitudes towards nutrition…

items.title: The schism of strategic planning in the climate crisis
items.summary_raw: Strategic planning is traditionally defined as a broader, more flexible process compared to statutory spatial planning. It most often involves investments and partnerships in urban development projects, increasing carbon emissions as a result. This creates a schism between the stated sustainable development objectives and the actual consequences of strategic planning. This study first tracked this schism in academic discourse across three different approaches to strategic planning. It revealed that the focus on ‘strategic’ in planning literature contrasts with the urgent commitments required for climate change mitigation. Second, the study investigated how this schism manifests in the two case studies of the tourism strategy and mobility planning in Copenhagen, Denmark. Given their significant role in urban development, tourism and mobility planning have major consequences for carbon emissions. Through a critical policy analysis, the case studies reveal how the schism unfolded – not only as a schism between vision and practice but also as contradictions within policy documents. The findings highlight the critical need to rethink strategic planning to effectively address the challenges of the climate crisis. Effective climate change mitigation requires a fundamentally different kind of strategic planning that is focused on reducing activities that produce carbon emissions.

items.title: Drivers of consumer acceptance of sea fennel food products
items.summary_raw: Sea fennel ( Crithmum maritimum L .) is a halophyte with notable nutritional and functional properties – including high content of essential oils, polyphenols, and minerals – that make it a promising climate-resilient ingredient for sustainable food product development. Despite this potential, consumer acceptance remains largely unexplored, representing a key barrier to its market integration. This study investigates the factors driving consumers’ intention to purchase sea fennel-based foods, applying an extended Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) framework enriched with food-related lifestyle variables. An online survey was conducted across five Mediterranean countries — Croatia, France, Italy, Tunisia, and Turkey — involving more than 1000 household food purchasers. .Subjective norm and attitude emerged as the strongest predictors of behavioural intention, with coefficients of comparable magnitude. Attitude was, in turn, mainly influenced by perception. Perceived behavioural control also contributed to shaping behavioural intention, although to a lesser extent. Food-related lifestyle exerted an additional direct influence, reflecting the role of broader dietary habits, personal values, and openness to novel foods. Low awareness and limited prior experience with sea fennel were identified as key constraints to acceptance. These findings carry direct implications for food producers, retailers, and policymakers: fostering familiarity through tasting initiatives, targeted…

items.title: The Shifting Narrative of a Scottish Sandstorm in Time
items.summary_raw: This work explores the shifting narrative of the Culbin disaster, a series of storm events in 1694 that caused severe damage to a local community, with attention to the changes of that narrative over time. It highlights several major themes including how the human element of Culbin, despite being documented in the first accounts of the events, has come and gone from the narrative, the emphasis on the storm itself, the spiritual element of early modern disasters, the power of nature, Culbin as a symbol of triumph, and anxieties of climate change. Culbin serves as a long-term study of a disaster and explores how people chose to remember it.

items.title: Can community energy become nuclear?
items.summary_raw: Community energy projects are typically associated with renewable, local, democratic and decentralised initiatives. The emergence of Small Modular Reactors and Microreactors challenges this historical gap between nuclear energy and energy communities by raising the possibility that nuclear technologies could effectively become part of community-oriented energy transitions. This Perspective argues that closing this gap cannot rely on modularity, smaller scale, technical, or even economic compatibility alone. Instead, it requires the construction of social embeddedness through credible safety and security, locally grounded knowledge and trust, and risk perceptions connected to community-valued strategic goals. Without these conditions, community nuclear energy risks becoming symbolic, thereby reproducing the historical separation of communities from nuclear energy and associated technologies.

items.title: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and the Theory of Planned Behavior to Explain Electric Vehicle Purchase Intention Through Willingness to Pay
items.summary_raw: This study examines the determinants of electric vehicle (EV) purchase intention in Indonesia by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) through attitude and willingness to pay (WTP) as sequential mediating mechanisms. Addressing inconsistent empirical findings in prior literature regarding ease of use, infrastructure, and green lifestyle, this research offers novelty by combining psychological evaluations and financial commitments into a unified framework. A quantitative approach was applied using purposive sampling, collecting primary data via an online survey targeting Indonesian individuals aged 17 and older who are familiar with EVs and possess potential purchase interest. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) via SmartPLS 4. The model demonstrates strong predictive power, explaining variance in attitude (R2 = 0.631), WTP (R2 = 0.628), and purchase intention (R2 = 0.707) The main findings reveal that attitude and WTP significantly drive purchase intention. Subjective norm, perceived usefulness, and battery warranty positively shape attitude, while price perception and perceived behavioral control enhance WTP. Conversely, perceived ease of use and charging infrastructure show no significant direct impacts, whereas green lifestyle and battery warranty negatively affect WTP. Theoretically, this study extends TAM and TPB by framing WTP as an economic bridge transforming…

items.title: The unequal flight: Policy design and public support for carbon taxation of air travel
items.summary_raw: Air travel is a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas emissions, yet policies to curb demand have remained politically contentious. We examine how policy designs and individual characteristics shape support for a carbon tax on air travel in Denmark. Using a preregistered discrete-choice experiment ( N = 1000), with an intentional oversample of high-income individuals, respondents evaluated air travel tax policies varying in tax level, revenue use, and frequent-flyer levy. Information about air travel and its climate impact was randomly assigned. Overall support was modest and highly sensitive to policy design. Higher tax levels substantially reduced support, whereas earmarking revenues for green initiatives increased it. Climate concern strongly predicted support for stringent and progressive designs, while it was lower among high-income individuals and frequent flyers. The information treatment had no significant effect on overall policy support. However, respondents for whom the information was novel expressed greater support. The treatment also increased the preference for policy designs that included a frequent-flyer levy.

items.title: Climate Responsive Interior Framework for Wildlife Hospitality in Ranthambore
items.source_name: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
items.summary_raw: Ranthambore is a distinctive wildlife tourism landscape shaped by its climate, ecology, cultural traditions and royal heritage. While its historic architecture demonstrates climate-responsive strategies involving heat management, shade, water, materials and spatial planning, contemporary luxury wildlife resorts do not always reflect these place-specific principles. This study examines the gap between Ranthambore’s traditional climate-responsive built environment and the design of contemporary hospitality interiors, particularly in relation to ecological identity, cultural authenticity and guest experience. The research aims to develop a climate-responsive interior design framework for wildlife hospitality in Ranthambore by identifying principles that can be meaningfully reinterpreted within contemporary luxury interiors. A qualitative research methodology is adopted, incorporating historical research, literature review, case studies and comparative analysis. The study examines climate-responsive design strategies, regional materials and crafts, ecological practices, community participation and guest education, while drawing upon traditional ecological knowledge and conservation practices of Rajasthan. The findings indicate that climate responsiveness and sustainability can extend beyond technological interventions to include material selection, spatial experience, local craftsmanship, cultural narratives, community engagement and interpretation of the landscape. Based on…

items.title: Social–ecological systems adaptation and response to climate variability in Africa: a scoping review
items.summary_raw: Climate variability is intensifying across Africa, disrupting the delicate balance of interconnected human and environmental systems. While adaptation is urgently needed to protect livelihoods and biodiversity, evidence regarding which strategies work, and under what conditions, remains fragmented. This scoping review utilizes a social, ecological systems (SES) lens to synthesize documented adaptation strategies and their reported social and ecological outcomes. Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we systematically searched academic databases and grey literature for studies on African SES adaptation published through June 2025. Out of 61 identified records, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning agricultural, water, fisheries, and urban systems. Data were extracted and analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis to identify recurring themes in strategies, governance, and outcomes. Based on the 35 included studies, the review identifies three primary clusters of adaptation: institutional (e.g., policy mainstreaming, co-management), behavioral (e.g., Indigenous knowledge, livelihood diversification), and technological (e.g., climate-resilient inputs, water–soil engineering). Results suggest that synergies between social and ecological outcomes are documented more frequently than trade-offs, especially in interventions involving nature-based solutions and integrated land–water planning. Reported adaptation effectiveness was frequently associated with hybrid…

items.title: How Wisconsin Extension Educators Talk About Climate Change Without Talking About ``Climate Change''
items.summary_raw: Climate change touches all areas of Extension's programming. To understand how educators approach talking about climate change with constituents, we interviewed 15 Extension educators and three program managers in Wisconsin. Crops and Soils educators view climate change as interwoven with their work, Financial Education educators view it as mostly disconnected, and Community Economic Development educators range between these extremes. Educators in all three programs avoid the polarizing phrase ``climate change,'' instead focusing on specific, local, and relatable issues. Educators show empathy and emphasize resilience (adaptation) rather than mitigation. These findings can inform Extension's organizational strategy on climate change.

items.title: Comparative energy justice scholarship: Toward an empirical research agenda
items.summary_raw: Drawing on our collective experiences conducting empirical research on the energy transition from fossil fuels to clean energy in select democracies in North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia, we propose a rich empirical approach that focuses on in-depth qualitative analysis to create a Comparative Energy Justice research agenda. The energy transition makes room for a more as well as less just system to emerge. Focusing on the energy transition rather than the broader category of energy allows us to center this interaction and provide insights for those advocating for greater energy justice. Each section summarizes findings and concludes with suggestions for comparative research. We first discuss political institutional structures related to energy policy that have been under-explored in energy justice research, notably federalism, public utility commissions, and Indigenous Nations governance. Next, we elaborate five categories of under-researched actors in the energy transition: the European Union's Local Action Groups, social justice organizations, businesses and political conservatives, faith-based organizations, and workers in the energy transition. Research should explore how these actors have interacted and will interact in the future with older coalition members who might have different experiences and world views. Moving beyond extant research that focuses on concepts and theoretical framing, our research agenda seeks to understand what is happening on the…

items.title: Assessing information security policy compliance: a managerial perspective on leadership and awareness
items.summary_raw: Purpose Insider non-compliance with information security policies (ISPs) remains a significant organisational risk. This study aims to examine how leadership styles and information security awareness (ISA) dimensions influence employees’ social cognitive beliefs (SCBs) and, ultimately, their information security policy compliance (ISPC) intention. Design/methodology/approach Guided by the theory of planned behaviour (TPB), a quantitative survey was conducted among professionals working in organisations with established ISPs. A total of 205 valid responses were analysed. Findings Attitude was the only TPB construct that significantly predicted ISPC intention. Ethical leadership emerged as the most consistent predictor of employees’ SCBs, whereas transformational leadership positively influenced subjective norms and self-efficacy. Transactional leadership showed no significant effects. Among the ISA dimensions, awareness of the benefits of security countermeasures positively influenced attitude, susceptibility awareness positively influenced self-efficacy and severity awareness negatively influenced self-efficacy. Research limitations/implications Due to the relatively small sample size and the predominance of South African participants, the results may not be fully applicable to larger populations. Practical implications Organisations should prioritise ethical leadership and benefit-oriented security awareness initiatives to strengthen employee compliance intentions. Social…

Climate governance as a determinant of climate change disclosure quality: Evidence from African listed firms
items.summary_raw: Climate change disclosure quality is important for assessing how firms identify, manage, and communicate climate-related risks and opportunities, yet evidence on governance mechanisms that support high-quality disclosure remains limited in African capital markets. This study examines the effect of climate governance on climate change disclosure quality among listed firms in nine African countries. Guided by the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework, disclosure quality is measured using a weighted index of eleven TCFD-aligned disclosures. Climate governance is measured using a composite index of risk management, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and environmental committees, together with executive climate incentives. Data for 137 firms from 2017 to 2025 were collected through content analysis and structured into an unbalanced panel that was analysed using the two-step System Generalised Method of Moments estimator. The results show that climate governance improves disclosure quality. Further analysis shows that CSR and environmental committees improve disclosure quality, while similar evidence is not established for risk management committees and executive climate incentives. The study contributes evidence on the collective and individual effects of climate governance on TCFD-aligned disclosure quality in a climate-vulnerable African context. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening climate governance structures to support…

items.title: When climate risk intensifies, does insurance pay off? A community case study of China's agricultural insurance reform
items.summary_raw: In the context of mounting global climate threats, fostering resilience in food production systems has become a critical imperative for upholding national food security. This paper exploits the staggered implementation, beginning in 2018, of China's agricultural insurance reforms covering full production costs and planting income as a quasi-natural experiment. Drawing on provincial panel data from 2013 to 2024, we first develop a multidimensional composite index to capture food production resilience. A staggered difference-in-differences specification is then adopted to systematically assess the causal effect of these reforms on such resilience and to explore the underlying transmission channels. Moreover, from a novel climate change perspective, the analysis examines the heterogeneous treatment effects across varying degrees of climate risk exposure. The empirical findings reveal that the policy-led agricultural insurance reform significantly and robustly enhances China's food production resilience. Mechanism tests indicate that advances in agricultural technology and the expansion of large-scale farming operations serve as important pathways through which the insurance policy takes effect. Further investigation shows that climate change risk positively moderates the policy impact: as climate risk intensifies, the marginal contribution of insurance to resilience becomes stronger. Heterogeneity analysis also demonstrates that the policy effect is more pronounced in western…

items.title: Hrozí České republice desertifikace?
items.summary_raw: Na otázku, zda Česku hrozí dezertifikace a co tento výraz vlastně znamená, odpovídal pro časopis Úroda i Zdeněk Žalud. Více čtěte zde.

items.title: Mitigation Without Adaptation: Cryosphere Risk, Hydropower, and the Climate Policy Gap in Nepal
items.summary_raw: Background: Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet ranks among the countries most exposed to the impacts of climate change. Hydropower sits at the center of the country's economy and its climate mitigation strategy. This sector, however, faces growing risk from glacial retreat and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). Nepal has set ambitious climate targets, but a clear gap persists between these mitigation goals and the pace of adaptation efforts on the ground. Objective: This study examines the extent to which Nepal's climate policy instruments (NAPA, LAPA, Climate Change Policy, NDC, NAP) address cryosphere-driven risks to hydropower infrastructure and identifies barriers to effective adaptation planning. Methods: The study used a qualitative, desk-based approach. It combined a systematic literature review with documentary analysis of policy instruments and peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2025. The analysis was guided by socio-ecological systems theory, adaptive governance theory, and political ecology. Results: The findings reveal a clear imbalance. Nepal has strong mitigation commitments for hydropower expansion, including the NDC target of 15,000 MW by 2030, but adaptation measures remain fragmented. Glacier loss is accelerating, with Yala Glacier losing 1.28 m water equivalent in 2022–2023. GLOF events are also becoming more frequent, with four major events recorded between 2016 and 2025. Hydropower losses have…

items.title: Investigating the key drivers of carbon-free energy production: New evidence from EU countries
items.summary_raw: Traditional energy sources are harmful to the environment. As a result, many countries have been pushed to shift toward carbon-free alternatives. Yet the demand for cleaner energy often outstrips what is currently available. One reason is that empirical work on what drives carbon-free energy production remains limited and often superficial, making it hard to design effective policies. This paper helps fill that gap by looking at what drives three types of carbon-free energy: renewable, nuclear, and bioenergy, across the EU27 countries. Using annual data from 2005 to 2022, we apply a new approach that combines Markov Chain Monte Carlo-estimated Generalized Quantile Regression (MCMC-GQREG) with frequency-domain Granger causality. Our main findings are: (i) green taxation, green finance, green R&D, and digitalization all significantly increase production of the three carbon-free energy types; (ii) green taxes and green finance have stronger positive effects on nuclear energy, while green R&D does more for renewable energy; (iii) digitalization and resource efficiency work especially well for bioenergy, followed by renewables and then nuclear; (iv) GDP mostly harms carbon-free energy production, which signals a need for strategic policy changes. These results hold up under robustness checks and offer useful lessons for reaching the EU's net-zero goals under the European Green Deal.

items.title: Slovensku vysychají řeky i nádrže. Problémy má i největší zásobárna pitné vody
items.summary_raw: Slovensko se na konci září potýká s mimořádně rozsáhlým suchem. Téměř polovinu země trápí extrémní půdní sucho a nedostatek vody se neprojevuje také v řekách a vodních nádržích. Ovlivňuje dokonce už i zásobování pitnou vodou. Výraznější úlevu zřejmě nepřinese ani začátek října. Více o tématu píší novinky.cz zde.

items.title: How German electric utilities navigate sector coupling: strategy archetypes and industry implications
items.summary_raw: Sector coupling is widely regarded as a cornerstone of Europe's energy transition, yet research has often overlooked the strategic behaviour of electric utilities as key actors. This paper addresses this gap by analysing how different types of utilities strategically respond to increased sector coupling. Drawing on a literature review and 36 semi-structured interviews with senior energy professionals in Germany, we apply an integrated strategy lens combining resource-based and position-based perspectives. We identify five strategy archetypes – platform scalers, integrators, deployers, hedgers, rationalisers – and describe strategy choices across power-to-mobility, power-to-heat, and power-to-gas/liquids as a snapshot of the current energy transition phase. We found that five contextual factors shape electric utilities' sector coupling strategies: 1. the regional and infrastructural context utilities operate in, 2. the availability of suitable locations and the ability to provide flexibility in the portfolio, 3. the digitalisation maturity, 4. the timeline, and 5. the economic pressure under which utilities operate. Our findings suggest that utilities are actively shaping sector coupling trajectories through distinct and partly competing strategies, each associated with different sources of strategic value, pursued at different speeds across technologies. This heterogeneity underlines the importance of incorporating firm-level strategy into research, policy, and practice to…

items.title: How information format, climate attitudes, and trust shape consumer response to food carbon emission information
items.summary_raw: Consumers often underestimate the carbon emissions associated with their food choices, and carbon-emissions information is increasingly proposed as a way to close this knowledge gap. Yet evidence remains limited regarding how alternative information formats affect intended dietary choices and whether responses vary across consumers. We conduct a randomized online experiment comparing personalized carbon-emissions totals, generic food-category rankings, and their combination. We also examine heterogeneity in treatment effects by climate attitudes and explore whether reported trust and information internalization are associated with these differences. On average, all three formats produce negative estimated effects on projected emissions, with the largest point estimate observed for the ordinal ranking. Effects are highly heterogeneous: individuals with greater concern about climate change reduce projected emissions, whereas those with low concern show little response. Climate-concerned individuals also report greater trust in the personalized information and update their self-assessed emissions more closely toward the displayed estimates. The association between climate attitudes and information internalization is substantially attenuated after accounting for reported trust. Together, our findings demonstrate that responses to carbon-emissions information depend on both the format of the information and consumers' pre-existing climate attitudes, underscoring the importance of…

items.title: Evaluating on-line media and survey data to understand beliefs and sentiment associated with pastured and integrated poultry production among farmers and stakeholders
items.summary_raw: Commercial pastured and integrated poultry production (PIPP) represents an emerging area of poultry and crop production. As a “niche” area of commercial production, there is little overall knowledge about public opinion associated with PIPP. Here we utilized two complementary approaches to better understand current sentiment and associated challenges with PIPP-based production. Specifically, to understand farmer PIPP sentiment and challenges we surveyed commercial PIPP farmers. In parallel we captured stakeholder sentiment toward integrative farming (a slightly broader classification that includes PIPP) via the extraction of selected data (i.e., web-scraping) on the internet. The methodology combines web-scraping of various media and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to understand sentiment in a longitudinal fashion. Here we compared a farmer survey of 53 producers and 2,399 English language web-scraped online posts (e.g., from online forums, news sites, and blogs) from 1,089 unique authors between 2019 and 2021 to understand opinions of and experiences with PIPP. The survey data and online posts both highlighted soil health, animal welfare, and weed control as perceived benefits of PIPP. In addition, survey respondents identified food safety regulations or incidents, processing, and certifications as barriers to PIPP whereas these topics rarely appeared in online conversations (i.e., on-line discourse capturing news and social media). items.title: Can Beauty Save the World? A Multimethod Analysis of Regulatory Focus Appeals in Climate Change Advertising
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT This study investigates how organizations can strategically design climate change advertising to foster greater consumer involvement by comparing the effectiveness of promotion‐ and prevention‐focused advertising appeals. Using a sequential explanatory mixed‐methods design, a facial coding experiment revealed that promotion appeals reduced sadness, which in turn positively influenced attitudes toward the ad and increased climate change involvement. A follow‐up qualitative study with communication managers provides practical insights into how these findings can inform the design of climate change advertising campaigns. By identifying the affective mechanism through which promotion‐focused appeals enhance climate change involvement, this study advances research on green advertising and climate change advertising and offers evidence‐based guidance for organizations seeking to design advertising campaigns that more effectively involve consumers with climate change. As organizations increasingly rely on green advertising to support sustainability initiatives, understanding how to design communications that motivate meaningful climate action remains a critical challenge for both researchers and practitioners.

items.title: Carbon dioxide utilization: a review of technologies, barriers, and policies for its deployment
items.summary_raw: The ever-increasing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions primarily Carbon Dioxide (CO 2 ), are adversely impacting the climate at an unprecedented rate, leading to more frequent extreme climate events. Reducing GHG and counteracting climate change can be achieved by decarbonizing energy systems and challenging the status quo of current industrial practices of producing and consuming energy. One solution to reduce the GHG impact is to separate CO 2 from flue gases and use it as a raw material for industrial processes and products. However, despite growing research activity, many CCU pathways remain limited by high energy demand, economic constraints, low technology maturity, and uncertain environmental performance. Existing literature review studies often focus primarily on conversion processes while providing limited assessment of commercialization barriers, scalability, and policy requirements for deployment. Our review evaluates major current pathways for utilizing CO 2 in diverse fields, such as fuels, chemicals, carbonation, concrete curing, tertiary oil recovery, coal bed methane recovery, bio-products, and horticulture. The study shows the technological status, deployment barriers, lifecycle implications, market potential, and policy framework associated with these pathways based on recent scientific and industrial developments. The work indicates that CCU technologies can contribute to industrial decarbonization, particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. However, large-scale…

items.title: Advancing 100% renewable electricity in Tunisia: techno-economic pathways for integrating solar PV, hydropower, and pumped hydro energy storage
items.summary_raw: Introduction Although Tunisia has a large potential for renewable energy, it is still heavily reliant on traditional biomass and fossil fuels, with each resident consuming only 0.5 MWh of electricity annually. This low level of consumption highlights the need for a long-term electrification strategy that would enable a more significant energy transformation. Methods This study explores the path to 100% renewable energy by directing final consumption sectors toward electricity, using a daily energy balance model of Tunisia’s electrical future until 2050. Solar photovoltaic (PV) and hydroelectric power are modeled as primary energy sources, while pumped hydro energy storage (PHES) and transboundary electricity imports are used for system equilibrium. Two scenarios are analyzed for 2050, including three levels of electricity demand (2.6 and 9.1 MWh per inhabitant and annually), two hydroelectricity development trajectories (ambitious and established), and scenarios with or without electricity imports. Results The results show that solar photovoltaic energy is the main source of production in most scenarios, but PHES plays a crucial role in daily and seasonal equilibrium. According to the main theories put forth, the levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) ranges from 17 TND/KWh to 24 TND/KWh. The sensitivity analysis revealed that photovoltaic costs, actualization rates, and hydroelectricity production scenarios are economic determinants. These results show that Tunisia’s future…

items.title: A life cycle assessment and multi-regional adaptation pathways for Sargassum-based concrete as a low-carbon building material
items.summary_raw: This study develops the Sargassum-Based Concrete Integrated Carbon Evaluation Framework (SBC-ICEF) to assess the environmental implications of incorporating processed Sargassum particles into concrete for potential non-load-bearing wall applications in coastal China. Laboratory measurements are linked to production-stage carbon inventories and supplementary carbon-retention scenarios, with potential operational-energy effects discussed qualitatively, using 1 m 3 of concrete and a reference building as complementary functional units. Among four tested mixtures, 10% volumetric replacement of fine aggregate was selected as a representative compromise. Compared with the control, this mixture reduced density by 8.51% and thermal conductivity by 18.18%, achieving 0.72 W / ( m · K ) , while retaining a mean compressive strength of 30.9 MPa. Water absorption increased from 5.2% to 8.8%, highlighting the need for moisture-related performance assessment. The quantified Sargassum-processing inventory totalled 1.22 t C O 2 e per tonne of dry processed material, with drying contributing 49.18%. Scenario analysis examined processing-energy sources, transport, assessment horizons, and conditional biogenic-carbon retention, supplemented by Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation. The findings identify promising initial material properties and processing priorities, while incomplete experimental documentation, industrial inventories, and durability evidence constrain extrapolation. items.title: Assessing methane generation potential for energy substitution in Qatar’s natural-gas-based economy
items.summary_raw: This study presents a comprehensive national-scale assessment of biomethane potential from organic waste streams in Qatar, evaluating its impact on two strategic climate mitigation pathways: (1) sustainable energy in water supply and agriculture, and (2) potential natural-gas substitution in Qatar’s gas-to-liquids (GTL) industry. The work is motivated by the substantial generation of potentially suitable organic feedstocks in Qatar, favorable climatic conditions, and the country’s strong reliance on natural gas-to-energy conversion industry. Following a comprehensive screening process, 12 organic waste sub-categories were assessed. Agricultural waste accounted for the largest share of AD-suitable organic waste in Qatar (61%); yet food waste contributed the highest biomethane potential (53%). A baseline theoretical biomethane potential (TBMP) was estimated at 313.7 million m³ CH₄/y. In terms of offsetting energy demand in Qatar’s water supply sector, the corresponding net methane-derived electricity could fully offset current energy requirements for (1) groundwater-based irrigation or (2) the production of Treated Sewage Effluent (TSE) – as an alternative source of irrigation water. Alternatively, it can cover 29-57% of desalination energy demand. Corresponding gross avoided grid emissions were estimated at 0.147–0.416 Mt CO₂-eq/y for on-farm groundwater pumping and treatment, 0.046–0.091 Mt CO₂-eq/y for TSE production, and 0.609 Mt CO₂-eq/y for desalination. items.title: Empowering student-led climate solutions: the role of AI in STEAM education
items.summary_raw: This convergent mixed-methods study investigates the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into a university-level STEAM curriculum to empower students to design climate solutions. Combining quantitative survey data from 69 undergraduate students selected via a complete cohort census sampling approach (response rate: 84.1%) and multi-tiered purposive qualitative interviews with N = 25 participants ( N = 11 experts, N = 9 faculty members, and N = 5 student innovators), the findings indicate high technological familiarity and widespread adoption (100% AI tool use). Specifically, students reported the highest agreement for AI enhancing their creativity and learning independence (86.9%, M = 4.12), supporting their capacity to pivot from data collection to strategic solution design (73.9%, M = 3.78), and bolstering their perceived empowerment to propose climate solutions (76.8%, M = 3.84). Furthermore, self-reported student perceptions indicated that AI supported their critical thinking process (68.1%, M = 3.65), representing perceived cognitive scaffolding rather than an objective measure of skill performance. This supports the qualitative finding that AI acts as a “Complexity Mediator” in climate tasks. However, notable concerns were reported regarding accuracy (60.9%) and plagiarism (59.4%). To address this, the study proposes the AI-Empowered STEAM Climate Action Model (AISC-AM), a conceptual framework that structures STEAM as a Multi-Scalar Problem-Solving…

items.title: Toward Climate Change Resilience and the Carbon‐Neutral Transition in Emerging Economies Through Circular Technologies and Green Energy Transmission Systems
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Despite growing evidence on the environmental benefits of green innovation, empirical findings for emerging economies remain limited and inconclusive, particularly regarding the joint role of environmental patents and renewable energy in reducing carbon emissions. Given the rapid economic growth of these countries, it is important to understand how environmental patents and climate change mitigation technologies influence sustainable economic growth in emerging markets. Using robust heterogeneous panel estimation methods that account for cross‐sectional dependence, the results consistently show that green innovation, measured by environmental patents, and renewable energy support the carbon‐neutral transition by reducing carbon emissions in emerging economies. The findings demonstrate that while green innovations significantly reduce emissions, the emissions‐reducing impact of renewable energy adoption is quantitatively larger. In contrast, energy consumption remains an important contributor to emissions. Overall, the study highlights that promoting green innovation together with renewable energy adoption is important for supporting long‐term environmental sustainability and the transition to carbon neutrality in emerging economies.
